source.text: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת שְׁתַּ֗יִם לְמַלְכוּת֙ נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּ֔ר חָלַ֥ם נְבֻֽכַדְנֶצַּ֖ר חֲלֹמ֑וֹת וַתִּתְפָּ֣עֶם רוּח֔וֹ וּשְׁנָת֖וֹ נִהְיְתָ֥ה עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And in year two of [the] reign of Nebuchadnezzar dreamed Nebuchadnezzar dreams, and was troubled his spirit, and his sleep was [done] upon him.

en.L: And in the second year of the kingship of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams; and his spirit was disturbed, and his sleep was [gone] from him.
en.B: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams. His mind was so troubled that he could not sleep.
en.R: In Nebuchadnezzar's second year as king, he had some dreams. They worried him so much that he could not sleep.

fr.L: Et la deuxième année du règne de Nabuchodonosor, Nabuchodonosor eut des songes ; et son esprit fut troublé, et son sommeil [s’enfuit] loin de lui.
fr.B: La deuxième année du règne de Nabuchodonosor, Nabuchodonosor eut des songes. Il en eut l’esprit si troublé qu’il ne pouvait plus dormir.
fr.R: Pendant la deuxième année où il était roi, Nabuchodonosor a fait des rêves. Ces rêves l’ont tellement inquiété qu’il n’arrivait plus à dormir.

es.L: Y en el año segundo del reinado de Nabucodonosor, Nabucodonosor tuvo sueños; y su espíritu se turbó, y su sueño se [fue] de él.
es.B: En el segundo año del reinado de Nabucodonosor, Nabucodonosor tuvo unos sueños. Su mente quedó tan perturbada que no podía dormir.
es.R: Cuando Nabucodonosor llevaba dos años como rey, tuvo unos sueños. Le preocuparon tanto que no podía dormir.

decisions.choice: the second year of Nebuchadnezzar: about 603 BC
alternatives: a different count of the years, or stories first told separately
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar's second year was about 603 BC. Chapter 1 says that Daniel and his friends were trained for three years before they entered the king's service (1:5, 18), yet here they are already counted among the wise men (verse 13). The difference is usually explained by the way the years were counted: if the young men arrived in Nebuchadnezzar's year of accession, their third year of training could fall in his second full year. Others think that the stories of the book were first told separately. The text does not explain it.

decisions.choice: his sleep was done upon him: he could not sleep
alternatives: his sleep came over him again
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that his sleep "was" or "came to be" on him, an unusual phrase that most take to mean that sleep went from him (compare 6:19, where the king's sleep "fled from him"). The sense is that the dreams disturbed him so much that he lay awake.

decisions.choice: His mind was so troubled (B); They worried him so much (R)
decisions.reason: "Spirit" here is the king's inner self, so Balanced says "mind". Literal keeps "spirit". Readable and Balanced join the two halves of the verse to show that the trouble kept him awake (m2).

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ לִקְרֹ֨א לַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֜ים וְלָֽאַשָּׁפִ֗ים וְלַֽמְכַשְּׁפִים֙ וְלַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים לְהַגִּ֥יד לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חֲלֹמֹתָ֑יו וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ וַיַּֽעַמְד֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said the king to call to the magicians, and to the enchanters, and to the sorcerers, and to the Chaldeans, to tell to the king his dreams; and they came and stood before the king.

en.L: And the king said to call for the magicians and the enchanters and the sorcerers and the Chaldeans, that they might declare to the king his dreams; and they came and stood before the king.
en.B: So the king ordered that the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers and Chaldeans be summoned to tell the king what he had dreamed. They came and stood before the king.
en.R: So the king sent for his magicians, enchanters, sorcerers and astrologers. He wanted them to tell him what he had dreamed. They came and stood in front of him.

fr.L: Et le roi dit d’appeler les magiciens, les enchanteurs, les sorciers et les Chaldéens, pour qu’ils exposent au roi ses songes ; et ils vinrent et se tinrent devant le roi.
fr.B: Le roi fit donc appeler les magiciens, les enchanteurs, les sorciers et les Chaldéens, pour qu’ils lui disent ce qu’il avait rêvé. Ils vinrent et se présentèrent devant le roi.
fr.R: Alors le roi a fait venir ses magiciens, ses enchanteurs, ses sorciers et ses astrologues. Il voulait qu’ils lui disent ce qu’il avait rêvé. Ils sont venus et se sont présentés devant lui.

es.L: Y el rey mandó llamar a los magos, y a los encantadores, y a los hechiceros, y a los caldeos, para que declararan al rey sus sueños; y vinieron y se presentaron delante del rey.
es.B: Entonces el rey ordenó llamar a los magos, encantadores, hechiceros y caldeos para que le dijeran al rey lo que había soñado. Ellos vinieron y se presentaron ante el rey.
es.R: Entonces el rey mandó llamar a sus magos, encantadores, hechiceros y astrólogos. Quería que le dijeran lo que había soñado. Ellos vinieron y se presentaron ante él.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: here a class of experts, not the people as a whole
decisions.reason: "Chaldeans" is the name of the people who ruled Babylon in this period (5:30; 9:1). In Daniel 2-5 it also names a group of the king's experts, listed with the magicians and enchanters (2:2, 4, 5, 10; 4:4; 5:7, 11). Greek and Roman writers later used "Chaldeans" for Babylonian astrologers and diviners, and that is its sense here: men trained in the old learning of Babylon, its omens and the reading of the stars (1:4).

decisions.choice: magicians, enchanters, sorcerers: three kinds of court expert
decisions.reason: The magicians and the enchanters are named in 1:20. The sorcerers are people who practice witchcraft, a word used of Pharaoh's sorcerers (Exodus 7:11) and forbidden in Israel (Deuteronomy 18:10). The list shows that the king called every kind of expert he had. Each group keeps its own name here, since the exact differences between them are not certain.

decisions.choice: to tell the king his dreams: to tell him what he had dreamed
decisions.reason: The king does not ask them only to explain the dreams but to tell him the dreams themselves, as verses 5-9 make plain.

decisions.choice: the list kept at every level; Chaldeans (L, B), astrologers (R)
decisions.reason: The book's lists of experts are kept at every level, each with its own word. Where "Chaldeans" means a class of experts, Readable says "astrologers", as the terms for Daniel set (m1); where it means the people (5:30), Readable says "Babylonians".

decisions.choice: "hechiceros"; "caldeos" (L, B); "astrólogos" (R)
decisions.reason: Where the Chaldeans are a class of experts, R says "astrólogos" (as Isaiah 47:13); L and B keep "caldeos". "Hechiceros" as Exodus 7:11

source.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר לָהֶ֛ם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ חֲל֣וֹם חָלָ֑מְתִּי וַתִּפָּ֣עֶם רוּחִ֔י לָדַ֖עַת אֶֽת־הַחֲלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them the king, a dream I have dreamed, and was troubled my spirit to know the dream.

en.L: And the king said to them, "A dream I have dreamed, and my spirit is disturbed to know the dream."
en.B: The king said to them, "I have had a dream, and my mind is troubled. I want to know what the dream was."
en.R: The king said to them, "I had a dream, and it worries me. I want to know what it means."

fr.L: Et le roi leur dit : « J’ai eu un songe, et mon esprit est troublé pour connaître le songe. »
fr.B: Le roi leur dit : « J’ai eu un songe, et mon esprit est troublé. Je veux savoir ce qu’était ce songe. »
fr.R: Le roi leur a dit : « J’ai fait un rêve, et il m’inquiète. Je veux savoir ce qu’il veut dire. »

es.L: Y el rey les dijo: «He soñado un sueño, y mi espíritu se ha turbado por conocer el sueño».
es.B: El rey les dijo: «He tenido un sueño y estoy muy perturbado. Quiero saber qué soñé».
es.R: El rey les dijo: «Tuve un sueño, y me tiene preocupado. Quiero saber qué significa».

decisions.choice: to know the dream: to know the dream itself and its meaning
alternatives: the king had forgotten the dream
decisions.reason: The king's words could mean that he wants to understand the dream, or that he cannot remember it. Verses 5-9 show that he demands that the experts tell him the dream itself. Whether he had forgotten it or was testing them, the text does not say plainly; verse 9 suggests a test.

decisions.choice: I want to know what it means (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the king wants in the plainest way. Verse 5 makes clear that the king wants both the dream and its meaning.

source.text: וַֽיְדַבְּר֧וּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֛ים לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲרָמִ֑ית מַלְכָּא֙ לְעָלְמִ֣ין חֱיִ֔י אֱמַ֥ר חֶלְמָ֛א לְעַבְדָ֖ךְ וּפִשְׁרָ֥א נְחַוֵּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke the Chaldeans to the king [in] Aramaic: O king, forever live! Tell the dream to your servants, and the interpretation we will declare.

en.L: And the Chaldeans spoke to the king [in] Aramaic, "O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation."
en.B: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic, "O king, may you live forever! Describe the dream to your servants, and we will explain its meaning."
en.R: Then the astrologers answered the king in Aramaic, "Your Majesty, may you live forever! Tell us your dream, and we will explain what it means."

fr.L: Et les Chaldéens parlèrent au roi [en] araméen : « Ô roi, vis à jamais ! Dis le songe à tes serviteurs, et nous exposerons l’interprétation. »
fr.B: Les Chaldéens répondirent alors au roi en araméen : « Ô roi, puisses-tu vivre à jamais ! Raconte le songe à tes serviteurs, et nous en donnerons l’interprétation. »
fr.R: Alors les astrologues ont répondu au roi en araméen : « Ô roi, que tu vives pour toujours ! Raconte-nous ton rêve, et nous t’expliquerons ce qu’il veut dire. »

es.L: Y los caldeos hablaron al rey [en] arameo: «¡Oh rey, vive para siempre! Di el sueño a tus siervos, y declararemos la interpretación».
es.B: Entonces los caldeos le hablaron al rey en arameo: «¡Oh rey, que vivas para siempre! Cuéntales el sueño a tus siervos, y te explicaremos su interpretación».
es.R: Entonces los astrólogos le respondieron al rey en arameo: «¡Mi rey, que vivas para siempre! Cuéntanos tu sueño, y te explicaremos lo que significa».

decisions.choice: in Aramaic: the language of the book changes here
alternatives: a note to the reader, "[in] Aramaic:", marking the change of language only
decisions.reason: "In Aramaic" marks the change of language, as in Ezra 4:7-8: the Hebrew text runs to this word, and the speech that follows is in Aramaic. The book itself goes on in Aramaic, not only for the Chaldeans' speech but through to the end of chapter 7 (2:4-7:28), and returns to Hebrew at 8:1. Aramaic was the common language of the Babylonian and Persian empires (2 Kings 18:26; Ezra 4:7), and Jews of the exile spoke it. Why the book is written in two languages is not known. Jeremiah 10:11 is another verse in Aramaic.

decisions.choice: O king, live forever: the usual greeting at court
decisions.reason: This was the polite way to address a king, wishing him a long life and reign (3:9; 5:10; 6:7, 22; Nehemiah 2:3; 1 Kings 1:31).

decisions.choice: the interpretation: the explanation of what the dream means
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word *peshar* means the explanation of a dream or a hidden message. It runs through chapters 2, 4 and 5.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty (R); us (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "Your Majesty" for "O king", the way a king is addressed in English today, and "us" for the polite "your servants". Literal and Balanced keep "O king". Readable also calls the Chaldeans "astrologers", as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: "Ô roi" at Readable where the English Readable says "Your Majesty", for the whole book
decisions.reason: "Majesté" requires "vous", and the court speaks to the king with "tu" in this translation; "ô roi" keeps the courtesy and the singular, as the term sheet asks.

decisions.choice: "l'interprétation" (Literal, Balanced), "ce que cela veut dire" and the like (Readable) for peshar, and "le mystère" (L, B) / "le secret" (R) for raz, for the whole book
decisions.reason: The book's two key words for revelation keep one French word each at Literal and Balanced, as the term sheet sets them; Readable says what they mean.

decisions.choice: "¡Oh rey, vive para siempre!" (L); "¡Oh rey, que vivas para siempre!" (B); "¡Mi rey, que vivas para siempre!" (R)
decisions.reason: The court greeting, worded the same way throughout the book. "O king" is "oh rey" at L and B and "mi rey" at R, never "Majestad", as in Samuel; the officials speak to the king with "tú"

source.text: עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְכַשְׂדָּאֵ֔י מִלְּתָ֖א מִנִּ֣י אַזְדָּ֑א הֵ֣ן לָ֤א תְהֽוֹדְעוּנַּ֨נִי֙ חֶלְמָ֣א וּפִשְׁרֵ֔הּ הַדָּמִין֙ תִּתְעַבְד֔וּן וּבָתֵּיכ֖וֹן נְוָלִ֥י יִתְּשָׂמֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: Answering the king and saying to the Chaldeans: the word from me [is] firm; if not you make known to me the dream and its interpretation, limbs you will be made, and your houses a refuse heap will be made.

en.L: The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, "The word from me is firm: if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, into limbs you will be made, and your houses will be made a refuse heap.
en.B: The king replied to the Chaldeans, "My decision is firm: unless you tell me both the dream and its interpretation, you will be torn limb from limb, and your houses will be turned into rubbish heaps.
en.R: The king said to the astrologers, "I have made up my mind. You must tell me what I dreamed and what it means. If you do not, I will have you cut to pieces and your houses turned into piles of rubble.

fr.L: Le roi répondit et dit aux Chaldéens : « La parole de ma part est ferme : si vous ne me faites pas connaître le songe et son interprétation, vous serez mis en pièces, et vos maisons seront réduites en tas d’ordures.
fr.B: Le roi répondit aux Chaldéens : « Ma décision est prise : si vous ne me faites pas connaître le songe et son interprétation, vous serez mis en pièces, et vos maisons seront changées en tas de décombres.
fr.R: Le roi a dit aux astrologues : « Ma décision est prise. Vous devez me dire ce que j’ai rêvé et ce que cela veut dire. Sinon, je vous ferai couper en morceaux, et vos maisons seront transformées en tas de ruines.

es.L: Respondió el rey y dijo a los caldeos: «La palabra de mi parte es firme: si no me {{plural_you:dan|dais}} a conocer el sueño y su interpretación, {{plural_you:serán hechos|seréis hechos}} pedazos, y {{plural_you:sus casas|vuestras casas}} serán convertidas en un muladar.
es.B: El rey respondió a los caldeos: «Mi decisión es firme: si no me {{plural_you:dicen|decís}} el sueño y su interpretación, {{plural_you:serán despedazados|seréis despedazados}}, y {{plural_you:sus casas|vuestras casas}} serán convertidas en montones de escombros.
es.R: El rey les dijo a los astrólogos: «Ya lo he decidido. {{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} que decirme lo que soñé y lo que significa. {{plural_you:Si no lo hacen|Si no lo hacéis}}, {{plural_you:los|os}} haré cortar en pedazos y {{plural_you:sus casas|vuestras casas}} quedarán reducidas a escombros.

decisions.choice: answered and said: a way of introducing speech
decisions.reason: Aramaic often introduces speech with "answered and said", even where nothing has been asked (compare the Gospels' "answered and said"). It means simply "replied" or "said". The phrase recurs throughout Daniel 2-7.

decisions.choice: the word from me is firm: my decision has been made and will not change
alternatives: the matter has gone from me (I have forgotten it)
decisions.reason: The word *'azda'* is borrowed from Persian and means "certain" or "publicly known". So the phrase means that the king's order is settled (as in verse 8). An older reading took it as "the thing has gone from me", that is, the king has forgotten the dream, but the word does not mean that.

decisions.choice: limbs you will be made ... a refuse heap: torn apart, your houses destroyed
alternatives: your houses will be made dunghills
decisions.reason: These are the threats of an ancient king: the guilty were cut to pieces and their houses pulled down and made into dunghills or ruins (3:29; Ezra 6:11). The word for "refuse heap" is rare, and its exact sense, whether a heap of rubble or of dung, is not certain.

decisions.choice: replied (B); said (R)
decisions.reason: The idiom "answered and said" is kept at Literal. Balanced says "replied" and Readable "said" (m1); later verses follow the same pattern.

decisions.choice: "répondit et dit" at Literal, for the whole book; "répondit", "dit" or "prit la parole" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The Aramaic introduces speech with "answering and saying" even where nothing is answered; Literal keeps both verbs, as the English does, and the other levels use the one verb French needs.

decisions.choice: plural_you spans in the king's speech
decisions.reason: The king addresses the experts as a group, so every "you" takes plural_you through 2:5–9

source.text: וְהֵ֨ן חֶלְמָ֤א וּפִשְׁרֵהּ֙ תְּֽהַחֲוֺ֔ן מַתְּנָ֤ן וּנְבִזְבָּה֙ וִיקָ֣ר שַׂגִּ֔יא תְּקַבְּל֖וּן מִן־קֳדָמָ֑י לָהֵ֕ן חֶלְמָ֥א וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ הַחֲוֺֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And if the dream and its interpretation you declare, gifts and a reward and honor great you will receive from before me; therefore the dream and its interpretation declare to me.

en.L: But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, gifts and a reward and great honor you will receive from me. Therefore declare to me the dream and its interpretation."
en.B: But if you make known the dream and its interpretation, you will receive gifts and rewards and great honor from me. So tell me the dream and its interpretation."
en.R: But if you tell me the dream and explain it, I will give you gifts, rewards and great honor. So tell me what I dreamed and what it means."

fr.L: Mais si vous exposez le songe et son interprétation, vous recevrez de moi des dons, une récompense et un grand honneur. C’est pourquoi exposez-moi le songe et son interprétation. »
fr.B: Mais si vous me faites connaître le songe et son interprétation, vous recevrez de moi des cadeaux, des récompenses et de grands honneurs. Dites-moi donc le songe et son interprétation. »
fr.R: Mais si vous me dites ce que j’ai rêvé et si vous me l’expliquez, je vous donnerai des cadeaux, des récompenses et de grands honneurs. Alors dites-moi ce que j’ai rêvé et ce que cela veut dire. »

es.L: Pero si {{plural_you:declaran|declaráis}} el sueño y su interpretación, {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} de mí regalos, recompensa y gran honra. Por tanto, {{plural_you:declárenme|declaradme}} el sueño y su interpretación».
es.B: Pero si me {{plural_you:dan|dais}} a conocer el sueño y su interpretación, {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} de mí regalos, recompensas y grandes honores. Así que {{plural_you:díganme|decidme}} el sueño y su interpretación».
es.R: Pero si me {{plural_you:cuentan|contáis}} el sueño y {{plural_you:me lo explican|me lo explicáis}}, {{plural_you:les|os}} daré regalos, recompensas y grandes honores. Así que {{plural_you:díganme|decidme}} lo que soñé y lo que significa».

decisions.choice: gifts and a reward and great honor
decisions.reason: The king offers both the threat of verse 5 and a rich reward. The word for "reward" is rare and may be borrowed from Persian; it is used again in 5:17, where Daniel refuses such gifts.

decisions.choice: therefore: so, then
decisions.reason: The small word that begins the last sentence draws the conclusion: since the reward is so great, they should tell him.

decisions.choice: I will give you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes the king the one who gives, which is what "from before me" means.

source.text: עֲנ֥וֹ תִנְיָנ֖וּת וְאָמְרִ֑ין מַלְכָּ֕א חֶלְמָ֛א יֵאמַ֥ר לְעַבְד֖וֹהִי וּפִשְׁרָ֥ה נְהַחֲוֵֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: They answered a second [time] and saying: the king, the dream let him tell to his servants, and the interpretation we will declare.

en.L: They answered a second time and said, "Let the king say the dream to his servants, and the interpretation we will declare."
en.B: They answered a second time, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will make known its interpretation."
en.R: Again they said to the king, "Your Majesty, please tell us the dream. Then we will explain what it means."

fr.L: Ils répondirent une seconde fois et dirent : « Que le roi dise le songe à ses serviteurs, et nous exposerons l’interprétation. »
fr.B: Ils répondirent une seconde fois : « Que le roi raconte le songe à ses serviteurs, et nous lui en ferons connaître l’interprétation. »
fr.R: Ils ont répété au roi : « Ô roi, raconte-nous ton rêve, s’il te plaît. Ensuite, nous t’expliquerons ce qu’il veut dire. »

es.L: Respondieron por segunda vez y dijeron: «Diga el rey el sueño a sus siervos, y declararemos la interpretación».
es.B: Ellos respondieron por segunda vez: «Que el rey cuente el sueño a sus siervos, y le daremos a conocer su interpretación».
es.R: Otra vez le dijeron al rey: «Mi rey, por favor, cuéntanos el sueño. Después te explicaremos lo que significa».

decisions.choice: let the king tell his servants: polite speech to a king
decisions.reason: The experts address the king in the third person, as courtiers did, and call themselves "his servants".

decisions.choice: Your Majesty, please tell us (R)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the courtly third person into direct address, as in verse 4.

source.text: עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֔ר מִן־יַצִּיב֙ יָדַ֣ע אֲנָ֔ה דִּ֥י עִדָּנָ֖א אַנְתּ֣וּן זָבְנִ֑ין כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּ֣י חֲזֵית֔וֹן דִּ֥י אַזְדָּ֖א מִנִּ֥י מִלְּתָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Answering the king and saying: from certainty knowing I that time you [are] buying, because that you have seen that [is] firm from me the word.

en.L: The king answered and said, "I know for certain that you are buying time, because you see that the word from me is firm,
en.B: The king replied, "I know for sure that you are trying to gain time, because you see that my decision is final.
en.R: The king answered, "I know that you are trying to stall, because you see that I mean what I said.

decisions.reason: The king repeats his decision of verse 5.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end (L)
decisions.reason: The king's sentence runs on into verse 9, which explains why he will not tell them the dream, so Literal ends the verse with a comma. Balanced and Readable end the sentence here.

en.L: that if you do not make known to me the dream, there is one law for you. And you have agreed to speak a lying and corrupt word before me until the time changes. Therefore tell me the dream, so that I may know that its interpretation you can declare to me."

decisions.choice: one is your law: there is one sentence for all of you
decisions.reason: "Law" here is the king's decree, the sentence of verse 5. All of them face the same penalty if they fail.

decisions.choice: until the time is changed: until circumstances change
decisions.reason: The king suspects that the experts hope to wait until he forgets the matter or something else happens, perhaps even a change of king.

decisions.choice: tell me the dream, and I will know: the test of a true interpreter
decisions.reason: The king's demand is shrewd: anyone can invent an interpretation, but only someone who truly receives knowledge from the gods could tell him the dream. This sets up the story's point, that only the God of heaven reveals secrets (verses 27-28).

decisions.choice: lies and deceit (B); lies and to mislead me (R)
decisions.reason: "A lying and corrupt word" is put into plain English. Readable says "hoping that things will change" for "until the time changes" (m2).

decisions.choice: "una [sola] es la ley"
decisions.reason: Spanish needs "sola" for the sense "one and the same sentence"; it is bracketed at L

records.literal_gloss: They answered the Chaldeans before the king and saying, not there is a man on the dry land who [the] matter of the king will be able to declare, because that any king great and powerful a matter like this not he has asked of any magician and enchanter and Chaldean.

en.L: The Chaldeans answered before the king, saying, "There is not a person on the dry land who is able to declare the king's matter, because no king, great and powerful, has asked a thing like this of any magician or enchanter or Chaldean.
en.B: The Chaldeans answered the king, "There is no one on earth who can do what the king asks! No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter or Chaldean.
en.R: The astrologers replied, "Nobody on earth can do what you ask! No other king, however great and powerful, has ever asked a magician, an enchanter or an astrologer to do such a thing.

fr.L: Les Chaldéens répondirent devant le roi et dirent : « Il n’y a pas un homme sur la terre sèche qui puisse exposer l’affaire du roi, parce qu’aucun roi, grand et puissant, n’a demandé une chose pareille à aucun magicien, enchanteur ou Chaldéen.
fr.B: Les Chaldéens répondirent au roi : « Il n’y a personne sur la terre qui puisse faire ce que le roi demande ! Jamais aucun roi, si grand et si puissant soit-il, n’a demandé une telle chose à un magicien, à un enchanteur ou à un Chaldéen.
fr.R: Les astrologues ont répondu : « Personne au monde ne peut faire ce que tu demandes ! Jamais aucun autre roi, même très grand et très puissant, n’a demandé une chose pareille à un magicien, à un enchanteur ou à un astrologue.

es.L: Respondieron los caldeos delante del rey y dijeron: «No hay hombre sobre la tierra que pueda declarar el asunto del rey; porque ningún rey, grande y poderoso, ha preguntado cosa semejante a ningún mago, ni encantador, ni caldeo.
es.B: Los caldeos respondieron al rey: «¡No hay nadie en la tierra que pueda hacer lo que el rey pide! Ningún rey, por grande y poderoso que haya sido, ha pedido jamás algo así a ningún mago, encantador o caldeo.
es.R: Los astrólogos le respondieron: «¡Nadie en el mundo puede hacer lo que pides! Ningún otro rey, por grande y poderoso que fuera, le ha pedido jamás algo así a un mago, a un encantador o a un astrólogo.

decisions.choice: no man on the dry land: no human being anywhere
decisions.reason: "The dry land" means the whole earth where people live. The experts admit the limit of human skill, which prepares for verse 11 and for Daniel's answer in verses 27-28.

decisions.choice: magician, enchanter and Chaldean: the experts of verse 2
decisions.reason: The list repeats three of the four groups of verse 2.

decisions.choice: magician, enchanter, Chaldean (L, B); magician, enchanter, astrologer (R)
decisions.reason: The list is kept at every level, with "astrologer" at Readable for the class of experts, as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: "pas un homme" (Literal) for ʾenash, without a gender span; "personne" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The English has no gender span here, and "pas un homme sur la terre" is the ordinary French for "no one at all"; Balanced and Readable say "personne", which is already inclusive.

en.L: And the matter that the king asks is difficult, and there is no other who can declare it before the king except gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh."
en.B: What the king asks is too difficult. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, and they do not live among human beings."
en.R: What you ask is too hard. Only the gods could tell you, and they do not live among people."

fr.L: Et la chose que le roi demande est difficile, et il n’y a personne d’autre qui puisse l’exposer devant le roi, excepté les dieux, dont la demeure n’est pas avec la chair. »

es.R: Lo que pides es demasiado difícil. Solo los dioses podrían decírtelo, y ellos no viven entre la gente».

decisions.choice: gods: the gods as the experts believed in them
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans speak as polytheists of "gods" in the plural. Their words are true in a way they do not mean: only God can make the dream known, and he does reveal it, though he is the God of heaven (verse 28).

decisions.choice: whose dwelling is not with flesh: who do not live among mortals
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means human beings in their weakness and mortality (Genesis 6:3; Isaiah 40:6). The experts mean that the gods are far off and do not share their secrets with people.

decisions.choice: human beings (B); people (R)
decisions.reason: "Flesh" is given as "human beings" and "people", which is what it means here (m2). Literal keeps "flesh".

source.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֔ה מַלְכָּ֕א בְּנַ֖ס וּקְצַ֣ף שַׂגִּ֑יא וַאֲמַר֙ לְה֣וֹבָדָ֔ה לְכֹ֖ל חַכִּימֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Because of this the king was angry and furious greatly, and said to destroy all [the] wise men of Babylon.

en.L: Because of this the king was angry and very furious, and he said to destroy all the wise men of Babylon.
en.B: This made the king so angry and furious that he ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be put to death.
en.R: This made the king very angry. He ordered that all the wise men in Babylon be killed.

fr.L: À cause de cela, le roi se mit en colère et s’irrita fort, et il dit de faire périr tous les sages de Babylone.
fr.B: Le roi en fut si irrité et si furieux qu’il ordonna de faire mourir tous les sages de Babylone.
fr.R: Cela a mis le roi très en colère. Il a donné l’ordre de tuer tous les sages de Babylone.

es.L: Por esto el rey se enojó y se enfureció mucho, y mandó destruir a todos los sabios de Babilonia.
es.B: Esto hizo que el rey se enojara y se enfureciera tanto que ordenó dar muerte a todos los sabios de Babilonia.
es.R: Esto enojó muchísimo al rey, y ordenó que mataran a todos los sabios de Babilonia.

decisions.choice: the wise men of Babylon: all the king's experts
decisions.reason: "Wise men" is the general name for all the groups listed in verse 2, the learned men of the royal court. Daniel and his friends are counted among them (verse 13).

decisions.choice: to destroy: to have them executed
decisions.reason: Ancient kings had the power to put their own officials to death, and such purges of court experts are known from other ancient sources. The order fulfills the threat of verse 5.

decisions.choice: put to death (B); be killed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say plainly that "destroy" here means "put to death".

records.literal_gloss: And the decree went out, and the wise men [were] being killed, and they sought Daniel and his companions to be killed.

en.L: And the decree went out, and the wise men were to be killed; and they sought Daniel and his companions to kill [them].
en.B: So the decree was issued that the wise men were to be killed, and they looked for Daniel and his friends to kill them.
en.R: So the order was given to kill the wise men. And men were sent to find Daniel and his friends to kill them too.

fr.L: Et le décret sortit, et les sages allaient être tués ; et on chercha Daniel et ses compagnons pour [les] tuer.
fr.B: Le décret fut donc publié : les sages devaient être mis à mort, et l’on chercha Daniel et ses compagnons pour les tuer.
fr.R: L’ordre a donc été donné de tuer les sages. Et des hommes ont été envoyés pour trouver Daniel et ses amis afin de les tuer eux aussi.

es.L: Y salió el decreto, y los sabios iban a ser muertos; y buscaron a Daniel y a sus compañeros para matarlos.
es.B: Así que se publicó el decreto de que los sabios debían morir, y buscaron a Daniel y a sus compañeros para matarlos.
es.R: Así que se dio la orden de matar a los sabios. Y enviaron hombres a buscar a Daniel y a sus amigos para matarlos también.

decisions.choice: were being killed: were about to be killed
decisions.reason: The verb form can mean that the killing had begun or that it was about to begin. Verse 24, where Daniel asks Arioch not to kill the wise men, suggests that it had not yet been carried out.

decisions.choice: Daniel and his companions: they were counted among the wise men
decisions.reason: Daniel and his friends were not called before the king in verse 2, but as members of the class of wise men they fell under the decree (1:20).

decisions.choice: men were sent to find ... too
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain who "they" were, the king's officers, and adds "too".

records.literal_gloss: Then Daniel returned counsel and discretion to Arioch, chief of the executioners of the king, who went out to kill the wise men of Babylon.

en.L: Then Daniel responded with counsel and discretion to Arioch, the chief of the king's executioners, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
en.B: Then Daniel spoke with wisdom and tact to Arioch, the commander of the king's guard, who had gone out to put the wise men of Babylon to death.
en.R: Arioch was the commander of the king's guard. He went out to kill the wise men of Babylon. But Daniel spoke to him wisely and politely.

fr.L: Alors Daniel répondit avec conseil et discernement à Aryok, le chef des exécuteurs du roi, qui était sorti pour tuer les sages de Babylone.
fr.B: Alors Daniel s’adressa avec sagesse et avec tact à Aryok, le commandant de la garde du roi, qui était sorti pour faire mourir les sages de Babylone.
fr.R: Aryok était le commandant de la garde du roi. Il est sorti pour tuer les sages de Babylone. Mais Daniel lui a parlé avec sagesse et politesse.

es.L: Entonces Daniel respondió con consejo y prudencia a Arioc, jefe de los verdugos del rey, que había salido para matar a los sabios de Babilonia.
es.B: Entonces Daniel habló con sabiduría y tacto a Arioc, comandante de la guardia del rey, que había salido a dar muerte a los sabios de Babilonia.
es.R: Arioc era el comandante de la guardia del rey. Había salido a matar a los sabios de Babilonia. Pero Daniel le habló con sabiduría y cortesía.

decisions.choice: chief of the executioners: commander of the royal guard
decisions.reason: The title means "chief of the slaughterers". It is the Aramaic form of the Hebrew title of Potiphar and of Nebuzaradan, "captain of the guard" (Genesis 37:36; 2 Kings 25:8). The commander of the king's bodyguard also carried out the king's sentences of death, which is what Arioch is doing here.

decisions.choice: returned counsel and discretion: answered wisely and tactfully
decisions.reason: Daniel does not panic or resist; he speaks with good sense and care for what is fitting. The same pairing of words for wisdom and judgment is used of wise speech in Proverbs.

decisions.choice: commander of the king's guard (B, R); chief of the king's executioners (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the title's form. Balanced and Readable give the office, as Balanced does in 2 Kings 25:8 ("captain of the guard"), since the title had come to mean the head of the royal guard (m1).

decisions.choice: "jefe de los verdugos del rey" (L); "comandante de la guardia del rey" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English levels; "Arioc" is the published form (Genesis 14:1)

records.literal_gloss: Answering and saying to Arioch, the officer of the king: on what [account is] the decree [so] urgent from before the king? Then the matter Arioch made known to Daniel.

en.L: He answered and said to Arioch, the king's officer, "Why is the decree from the king so urgent?" Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
en.B: He asked Arioch, the king's officer, "Why is the king's decree so urgent?" Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
en.R: He asked Arioch, "Why has the king given such a harsh order?" So Arioch told Daniel what had happened.

fr.L: Il répondit et dit à Aryok, l’officier du roi : « Pourquoi le décret du roi est-il si pressant ? » Alors Aryok fit connaître l’affaire à Daniel.
fr.B: Il demanda à Aryok, l’officier du roi : « Pourquoi le décret du roi est-il si urgent ? » Alors Aryok expliqua l’affaire à Daniel.
fr.R: Il a demandé à Aryok : « Pourquoi le roi a-t-il donné un ordre si dur ? » Alors Aryok a raconté à Daniel ce qui s’était passé.

es.L: Respondió y dijo a Arioc, oficial del rey: «¿Por qué es tan apremiante el decreto de parte del rey?». Entonces Arioc le dio a conocer el asunto a Daniel.
es.B: Le preguntó a Arioc, el oficial del rey: «¿Por qué es tan urgente el decreto del rey?». Entonces Arioc le explicó el asunto a Daniel.
es.R: Le preguntó a Arioc: «¿Por qué el rey ha dado una orden tan dura?». Entonces Arioc le contó a Daniel lo que había pasado.

decisions.choice: urgent: harsh, or hasty
decisions.reason: The word can mean "urgent" or "harsh, severe" (3:22 uses it of the king's urgent order). Daniel may be asking why the decree came so suddenly, or why it was so severe; both fit, and both suggest that he had not heard of the dream.

decisions.choice: the king's officer: a high official
decisions.reason: The word describes someone with authority, a captain or commander. Arioch is so called because he holds power to carry out the king's order.

decisions.choice: such a harsh order (R)
decisions.reason: Readable takes the sense "harsh", which Balanced's "urgent" also allows (m1).

records.literal_gloss: And Daniel went in and asked from the king that time he would give to him, and the interpretation to declare to the king.

en.L: And Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, and [he would] declare the interpretation to the king.
en.B: So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so that he might tell the king the interpretation.
en.R: So Daniel went to the king and asked him for more time. He promised that he would explain the dream to the king.

fr.L: Et Daniel entra et demanda au roi qu’il lui donne du temps, et [il] exposerait l’interprétation au roi.
fr.B: Daniel entra donc chez le roi et lui demanda de lui accorder du temps, pour qu’il puisse donner au roi l’interprétation.
fr.R: Alors Daniel est allé voir le roi et lui a demandé plus de temps. Il a promis qu’il expliquerait le rêve au roi.

es.L: Y Daniel entró y pidió al rey que le diera tiempo, y [que él] declararía la interpretación al rey.
es.B: Entonces Daniel entró y le pidió al rey que le diera tiempo para darle a conocer la interpretación.
es.R: Entonces Daniel fue a ver al rey y le pidió más tiempo. Le prometió que le explicaría el sueño.

decisions.choice: Daniel went in and asked the king: he made his request to the king
decisions.reason: The verse is short and does not say how Daniel reached the king. In verse 25 Arioch brings Daniel before the king as if he were new to him. The two may be told from different points of view: Daniel's request for time, perhaps through Arioch, and then his formal presentation. The text does not explain how they fit.

decisions.choice: time ... and the interpretation: Daniel trusts God before he knows the dream
decisions.reason: Unlike the Chaldeans, who were "buying time" (verse 8), Daniel asks for time in order to pray (verses 17-18). He promises an interpretation before he has received it.

decisions.choice: so that he might tell (B); He promised (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew joins the request and the promise with "and". Balanced and Readable say how the two relate.

source.text: אֱדַ֥יִן דָּֽנִיֵּ֖אל לְבַיְתֵ֣הּ אֲזַ֑ל וְ֠לַחֲנַנְיָה מִֽישָׁאֵ֧ל וַעֲזַרְיָ֛ה חַבְר֖וֹהִי מִלְּתָ֥א הוֹדַֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Then Daniel to his house went, and to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah his companions the matter he made known,

en.L: Then Daniel went to his house, and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah, his companions,
en.B: Then Daniel went home and told his friends Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah what had happened.
en.R: Then Daniel went home. He told his friends Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah what had happened.

fr.L: Alors Daniel alla à sa maison, et il fit connaître l’affaire à Hanania, Mishaël et Azaria, ses compagnons,
fr.B: Puis Daniel rentra chez lui et mit au courant ses compagnons Hanania, Mishaël et Azaria.
fr.R: Ensuite, Daniel est rentré chez lui. Il a raconté à ses amis Hanania, Mishaël et Azaria ce qui s’était passé.

es.L: Entonces Daniel fue a su casa, y dio a conocer el asunto a Hananías, Misael y Azarías, sus compañeros,
es.B: Luego Daniel se fue a su casa y les contó a sus amigos Hananías, Misael y Azarías lo que había pasado.
es.R: Después Daniel se fue a su casa y les contó a sus amigos Hananías, Misael y Azarías lo que había pasado.

decisions.choice: Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah: the Hebrew names of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego
decisions.reason: Here, among themselves, the friends are called by their Hebrew names, as in chapter 1; in verse 49 and in chapter 3, at the king's court, they are called by their Babylonian names (1:7).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end (L)
decisions.reason: The sentence runs on into verse 18, which says why Daniel told them, so Literal ends the verse with a comma. Balanced and Readable end the sentence here.

source.text: וְרַחֲמִ֗ין לְמִבְעֵא֙ מִן־קֳדָם֙ אֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א עַל־רָזָ֖ה דְּנָ֑ה דִּ֣י לָ֤א יְהֹֽבְדוּן֙ דָּנִיֵּ֣אל וְחַבְר֔וֹהִי עִם־שְׁאָ֖ר חַכִּימֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And compassion to seek from before [the] God of the heavens concerning this secret, that not they would destroy Daniel and his companions with [the] rest of [the] wise men of Babylon.

en.L: and [told them] to seek compassion from the God of heaven concerning this secret, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
en.B: He urged them to ask the God of heaven for mercy concerning this mystery, so that he and his friends would not be put to death with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
en.R: He asked them to pray to the God of heaven to be kind to them and show them the secret. Then they would not be killed with the other wise men of Babylon.

fr.L: et [leur dit] de demander compassion au Dieu des cieux au sujet de ce mystère, afin que Daniel et ses compagnons ne périssent pas avec le reste des sages de Babylone.
fr.B: Il les pressa de demander au Dieu des cieux d’avoir compassion d’eux au sujet de ce mystère, pour que lui et ses compagnons ne soient pas mis à mort avec les autres sages de Babylone.
fr.R: Il leur a demandé de prier le Dieu du ciel pour qu’il soit bon avec eux et leur fasse connaître le secret. Ainsi, ils ne seraient pas tués avec les autres sages de Babylone.

es.L: y [les dijo] que pidieran misericordia del Dios de los cielos acerca de este misterio, para que Daniel y sus compañeros no fueran destruidos con el resto de los sabios de Babilonia.
es.B: Les pidió que suplicaran misericordia al Dios de los cielos acerca de este misterio, para que ni él ni sus amigos murieran junto con los demás sabios de Babilonia.
es.R: Les pidió que oraran al Dios de los cielos para que tuviera compasión de ellos y les mostrara el secreto. Así no los matarían junto con los otros sabios de Babilonia.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven: a title for Israel's God used in the Persian period
decisions.reason: This title is used in Ezra, Nehemiah and Daniel, books written for Jews living under foreign kings (Ezra 1:2; Nehemiah 1:4; Daniel 2:19, 37, 44). It names God in a way the nations could understand, as the one who rules from heaven over all, and it sets him above the gods of Babylon, which were linked with the stars.

decisions.choice: this secret: the hidden matter of the king's dream
decisions.reason: The word *raz* is borrowed from Persian and means a secret or mystery, something hidden that only God can reveal (verses 19, 27-30, 47; 4:6). It is the Aramaic word behind the later Greek "mystery".

decisions.choice: compassion: mercy, pity
decisions.reason: The word is plural, as often, and means God's tender mercy. They ask God to have mercy by revealing the secret, and so to save their lives.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven at every level
decisions.reason: The title is kept at every level, as in Ezra. Readable says what the mercy is: kindness shown by revealing the secret. Literal brackets "[told them]", since verse 18 continues the sentence of verse 17.

decisions.choice: "le Dieu des cieux" (Literal, Balanced), "le Dieu du ciel" (Readable), for the whole book
alternatives: "le Dieu du ciel" at every level
decisions.reason: As published Ezra, where the same Aramaic title is used: the plural "cieux" is the traditional form of the title, and Readable uses the everyday singular.

decisions.choice: "el Dios de los cielos"
decisions.reason: The title as published in 2 Chronicles 36:23 and Ezra; used throughout Daniel

source.text: אֱדַ֗יִן לְדָנִיֵּ֛אל בְּחֶזְוָ֥א דִֽי־לֵילְיָ֖א רָזָ֣ה גֲלִ֑י אֱדַ֨יִן֙ דָּֽנִיֵּ֔אל בָּרִ֖ךְ לֶאֱלָ֥הּ שְׁמַיָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Then to Daniel in the vision of the night the secret was revealed. Then Daniel blessed the God of the heavens.

en.L: Then the secret was revealed to Daniel in the vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
en.B: Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision during the night, and Daniel praised the God of heaven.
en.R: That night God showed Daniel the secret in a vision. Then Daniel praised the God of heaven.

fr.L: Alors le mystère fut révélé à Daniel dans la vision de la nuit. Alors Daniel bénit le Dieu des cieux.
fr.B: Alors le mystère fut révélé à Daniel dans une vision pendant la nuit, et Daniel loua le Dieu des cieux.
fr.R: Cette nuit-là, Dieu a montré le secret à Daniel dans une vision. Alors Daniel a loué le Dieu du ciel.

es.L: Entonces el misterio le fue revelado a Daniel en visión de noche. Entonces Daniel bendijo al Dios de los cielos.
es.B: Entonces el misterio le fue revelado a Daniel en una visión durante la noche, y Daniel alabó al Dios de los cielos.
es.R: Esa noche Dios le mostró a Daniel el secreto en una visión. Entonces Daniel alabó al Dios de los cielos.

decisions.choice: the vision of the night: a revelation that came at night
decisions.reason: The book does not say whether Daniel was asleep and dreaming or awake. The phrase is used again of Daniel's own visions (7:2, 7, 13).

decisions.choice: blessed: praised, gave thanks
decisions.reason: When people "bless" God, they speak well of him and thank him, as Daniel does in verses 20-23.

decisions.choice: God showed Daniel (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says the secret "was revealed", without naming who revealed it. Readable names God, which the hymn makes plain (verses 22-23, 28).

source.text: עָנֵ֤ה דָֽנִיֵּאל֙ וְאָמַ֔ר לֶהֱוֵ֨א שְׁמֵ֤הּ דִּֽי־אֱלָהָא֙ מְבָרַ֔ךְ מִן־עָלְמָ֖א וְעַ֣ד־עָלְמָ֑א דִּ֧י חָכְמְתָ֛א וּגְבוּרְתָ֖א דִּ֥י לֵֽהּ־הִֽיא׃

records.literal_gloss: Answering Daniel and saying: let be the name of God blessed from the age and to the age, for wisdom and might, which [are] to him, it.

en.L: Daniel answered and said: \q "Let the name of God be blessed \q from everlasting to everlasting, \q for wisdom and might are {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}.
en.B: Daniel said: \q "Blessed be the name of God \q from age to age, \q for wisdom and power belong to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Daniel said: \q "Praise God forever and ever! \q He is wise and powerful.

fr.L: Daniel répondit et dit : \q « Que le nom de Dieu soit béni \q d’éternité en éternité, \q car la sagesse et la puissance sont à {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Daniel dit : \q « Béni soit le nom de Dieu \q d’âge en âge, \q car la sagesse et la force {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} appartiennent.
fr.R: Daniel a dit : \q « Louez Dieu pour toujours et à jamais ! \q Il est sage et puissant.

es.L: Daniel respondió y dijo: \q «Sea bendito el nombre de Dios \q desde la eternidad y hasta la eternidad, \q porque la sabiduría y el poder son {{deity_pronoun:suyos|Suyos}}.
es.B: Daniel dijo: \q «Bendito sea el nombre de Dios \q de una época a otra, \q porque a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} pertenecen la sabiduría y el poder.
es.R: Daniel dijo: \q «¡Alaben a Dios por siempre y para siempre! \q Él es sabio y poderoso.

decisions.choice: the start of a hymn: verses 20-23 are Daniel's song of praise
decisions.reason: Daniel's answer to the revelation is a poem of praise in four verses, built of parallel lines, the first of several hymns in the stories of the book (3:31-33; 4:31-32; 6:27-28). It praises God for the very gifts the experts lacked: wisdom, power, and the knowledge of hidden things.

decisions.choice: the name of God: God himself as he has made himself known
decisions.reason: To bless God's name is to praise God himself. The phrase is common in the Psalms (Psalm 113:2; Job 1:21).

decisions.choice: from age to age: forever
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says "from the age and to the age", that is, for all time past and to come (compare Psalm 41:14; 106:48).

decisions.choice: set in lines; the hymn in quotation marks
decisions.reason: Daniel's hymn is set in lines, following the Aramaic accents, with the opening words as its first line. Like Jonah's psalm (Jonah 2:3), it is a song quoted in a story, so it takes quotation marks. Readable says "forever and ever" for "from age to age" (m3), and turns "wisdom and might are his" into "He is wise and powerful".

decisions.choice: the hymn (2:20-23) is speech: present and passé composé at every level, in « » from its first line
alternatives: passé simple for the past within the hymn
decisions.reason: Daniel's praise is quoted speech, so French uses the tenses of speech, as in the Psalms; the narrative frame keeps the passé simple at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: lines and « » for the hymn
decisions.reason: Daniel's song of praise (2:20–23) is set in lines like the English; the quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 23

source.text: וְ֠הוּא מְהַשְׁנֵ֤א עִדָּנַיָּא֙ וְזִמְנַיָּ֔א מְהַעְדֵּ֥ה מַלְכִ֖ין וּמְהָקֵ֣ים מַלְכִ֑ין יָהֵ֤ב חָכְמְתָא֙ לְחַכִּימִ֔ין וּמַנְדְּעָ֖א לְיָדְעֵ֥י בִינָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he changes the times and the seasons, removes kings and sets up kings; gives wisdom to wise men and knowledge to those knowing understanding.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} changes the times and the set seasons; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} removes kings and raises up kings; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} grants wisdom to the wise \q and knowledge to those who know discernment.
en.B: He changes times and seasons; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deposes kings and installs kings. \q He gives wisdom to the wise \q and knowledge to those with insight.
en.R: He controls the times and seasons. \q He removes kings and puts others in their place. \q He gives the wise their wisdom \q and gives knowledge to people who understand.

fr.L: C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui change les temps et les saisons fixées ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} renverse les rois et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} établit les rois ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne la sagesse aux sages \q et la connaissance à ceux qui connaissent le discernement.
fr.B: Il change les temps et les saisons ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} renverse les rois et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les remplace. \q Il donne la sagesse aux sages \q et la connaissance à ceux qui ont de l’intelligence.
fr.R: C’est {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} qui décide des moments et des saisons. \q Il enlève le pouvoir aux rois et le donne à d’autres. \q Il donne aux sages leur sagesse \q et donne la connaissance aux gens qui comprennent.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} cambia los tiempos y las épocas; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} quita reyes y pone reyes; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} da sabiduría a los sabios \q y conocimiento a los que saben entender.
es.B: Él cambia los tiempos y las estaciones; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} destituye reyes y pone reyes. \q Él da sabiduría a los sabios \q y conocimiento a los entendidos.
es.R: Él gobierna los tiempos y las épocas. \q Él quita a los reyes y pone a otros en su lugar. \q Él les da sabiduría a los sabios \q y conocimiento a quienes saben entender.

decisions.choice: he changes times and seasons, removes kings and sets up kings: God rules history
decisions.reason: The two lines state the theme of the whole book: kingdoms rise and fall at God's command, not by human power (2:37-45; 4:14, 22, 29; 5:21). The "times and seasons" are the set periods of history. The same words return in 7:25, where the arrogant king tries to change the times and the law.

decisions.choice: gives wisdom to the wise: wisdom is God's gift
decisions.reason: The wise do not earn wisdom by themselves; God gives it to them, as he gave it to Daniel and his friends (1:17). The line answers the failure of Babylon's wise men.

decisions.choice: controls (R); puts others in their place (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "controls" for "changes", since the point is God's rule over time, and makes "sets up kings" plain.

source.text: ה֛וּא גָּלֵ֥א עַמִּיקָתָ֖א וּמְסַתְּרָתָ֑א יָדַע֙ מָ֣ה בַחֲשׁוֹכָ֔א וּנְהוֹרָ֖א עִמֵּ֥הּ שְׁרֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: He reveals the deep [things] and the hidden [things]; he knows what [is] in the darkness, and the light with him dwells.

en.L: He reveals the deep and the hidden [things]; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows what [is] in the darkness, \q and the light abides with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He reveals deep and hidden things; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knows what is in the darkness, \q and light lives with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: He shows people deep secrets that are hidden. \q He knows what is hidden in the dark, \q and light is all around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Il révèle les choses profondes et cachées ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sait ce qu’il [y a] dans les ténèbres, \q et la lumière demeure avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Il révèle les choses profondes et cachées ; \q {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sait ce qui se trouve dans les ténèbres, \q et la lumière habite auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.R: Il fait connaître aux gens des secrets profonds et cachés. \q Il sait ce qui est caché dans le noir, \q et la lumière est tout autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

es.L: Él revela lo profundo y lo escondido; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sabe lo que [hay] en las tinieblas, \q y la luz habita con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: Él revela las cosas profundas y ocultas; \q {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sabe lo que hay en la oscuridad, \q y la luz vive con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.R: Él muestra a la gente secretos profundos y escondidos. \q Él sabe lo que está oculto en la oscuridad, \q y la luz {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} rodea por todas partes.

decisions.choice: he reveals deep and hidden things: God knows and makes known what no one else can
decisions.reason: The line speaks directly of the secret of the king's dream: what is hidden from people is open to God, and he can make it known. The darkness is all that is hidden from human sight (Psalm 139:11-12).

decisions.choice: the light dwells with him: God is surrounded by light and sees all
decisions.reason: Light is a picture of God's presence and knowledge (Psalm 104:2; 1 Timothy 6:16). Darkness hides nothing from the one with whom the light lives. The written form of the text spells "light" with a slightly different form, but the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: shows people deep secrets (R); light is all around him (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "shows people" for "reveals" and joins "deep" and "hidden" into "deep secrets that are hidden". It gives "the light dwells with him" as a picture a young reader can see (m2).

source.text: לָ֣ךְ׀אֱלָ֣הּ אֲבָהָתִ֗י מְהוֹדֵ֤א וּמְשַׁבַּח֙ אֲנָ֔ה דִּ֧י חָכְמְתָ֛א וּגְבוּרְתָ֖א יְהַ֣בְתְּ לִ֑י וּכְעַ֤ן הֽוֹדַעְתַּ֨נִי֙ דִּֽי־בְעֵ֣ינָא מִנָּ֔ךְ דִּֽי־מִלַּ֥ת מַלְכָּ֖א הוֹדַעְתֶּֽנָא׃

records.literal_gloss: To you, God of my fathers, giving thanks and praising [am] I, for wisdom and might you have given to me, and now you have made known to me what we asked from you, for the matter of the king you have made known to us.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God of my fathers, I give thanks and praise, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me wisdom and might, \q and now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made known to me what we asked of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q for the king's matter {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made known to us."
en.B: To {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, God of my ancestors, I give thanks and praise, \q for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have given me wisdom and power. \q Now {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have shown me what we asked of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have made known to us what the king wanted to know."
en.R: God of my ancestors, I thank and praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}! \q You have made me wise and strong. \q You have told me what we asked {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q You have shown us the king's dream."

fr.L: À {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Dieu de mes pères, je rends grâce et je donne louange, \q car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as donné la sagesse et la puissance, \q et maintenant {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as fait connaître ce que nous {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons demandé, \q car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as fait connaître l’affaire du roi. »
fr.B: À {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, Dieu de mes ancêtres, je rends grâce et je chante ma louange, \q car {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as donné la sagesse et la force. \q Maintenant {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} m’as montré ce que nous {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons demandé ; \q {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} nous as fait connaître ce que le roi voulait savoir. »
fr.R: Dieu de mes ancêtres, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} remercie et je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} loue ! \q Tu m’as rendu sage et fort. \q Tu m’as dit ce que nous {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}avons demandé. \q Tu nous as fait connaître le rêve du roi. »

es.L: A {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, Dios de mis padres, doy gracias y alabo, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me has dado sabiduría y poder, \q y ahora me has dado a conocer lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pedimos, \q pues el asunto del rey nos has dado a conocer».
es.B: A {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, Dios de mis antepasados, te doy gracias y te alabo, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me has dado sabiduría y poder. \q Ahora me has mostrado lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pedimos; \q nos has dado a conocer lo que el rey quería saber».
es.R: ¡Dios de mis antepasados, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} doy gracias y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} alabo! \q Tú me has hecho sabio y fuerte. \q Me has dicho lo que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} pedimos. \q Nos has mostrado el sueño del rey».

decisions.choice: made known to me ... made known to us: Daniel received the answer for all four
decisions.reason: Daniel moves from "me" to "us": the answer came to him, but it was the prayer of all four friends (verses 17-18), and it saves their lives together.

decisions.choice: God of my fathers: the God of Israel's ancestors
decisions.reason: Daniel praises the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the God of his own people, not one of the gods of Babylon (compare Exodus 3:15).

decisions.choice: fathers (L); ancestors (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", the sense of "fathers" here. The hymn's quotation closes at the end of the verse.

source.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֣ל דְּנָ֗ה דָּֽנִיֵּאל֙ עַ֣ל עַל־אַרְי֔וֹךְ דִּ֚י מַנִּ֣י מַלְכָּ֔א לְהוֹבָדָ֖ה לְחַכִּימֵ֣י בָבֶ֑ל אֲזַ֣ל׀וְכֵ֣ן אֲמַר־לֵ֗הּ לְחַכִּימֵ֤י בָבֶל֙ אַל־תְּהוֹבֵ֔ד הַעֵ֨לְנִי֙ קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֔א וּפִשְׁרָ֖א לְמַלְכָּ֥א אֲחַוֵּֽא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Because of this Daniel went in to Arioch whom had appointed the king to destroy the wise men of Babylon; he went and thus said to him: the wise men of Babylon do not destroy; bring me in before the king, and the interpretation to the king I will declare.

en.L: Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had assigned to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and spoke to him thus, "The wise men of Babylon do not destroy. Bring me in before the king, and the interpretation I will declare to the king."
en.B: So Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to put the wise men of Babylon to death. He went and said to him, "Do not put the wise men of Babylon to death. Take me to the king, and I will tell the king the interpretation."
en.R: Then Daniel went to Arioch, the man the king had chosen to kill the wise men of Babylon. Daniel said to him, "Do not kill the wise men of Babylon. Take me to the king. I will explain his dream to him."

fr.L: C’est pourquoi Daniel entra auprès d’Aryok, que le roi avait chargé de faire périr les sages de Babylone. Il alla et lui parla ainsi : « Ne fais pas périr les sages de Babylone. Fais-moi entrer devant le roi, et j’exposerai l’interprétation au roi. »
fr.B: Daniel se rendit donc auprès d’Aryok, que le roi avait chargé de faire mourir les sages de Babylone. Il alla lui dire : « Ne fais pas mourir les sages de Babylone. Conduis-moi auprès du roi, et je lui donnerai l’interprétation. »
fr.R: Alors Daniel est allé voir Aryok, l’homme que le roi avait choisi pour tuer les sages de Babylone. Daniel lui a dit : « Ne tue pas les sages de Babylone. Emmène-moi chez le roi. Je lui expliquerai son rêve. »

es.L: Por esto Daniel entró a donde Arioc, a quien el rey había designado para destruir a los sabios de Babilonia. Fue y le dijo así: «No destruyas a los sabios de Babilonia. Llévame delante del rey, y yo le declararé al rey la interpretación».
es.B: Así que Daniel fue a ver a Arioc, a quien el rey había encargado dar muerte a los sabios de Babilonia. Fue y le dijo: «No mates a los sabios de Babilonia. Llévame ante el rey, y yo le diré al rey la interpretación».
es.R: Entonces Daniel fue a ver a Arioc, el hombre que el rey había escogido para matar a los sabios de Babilonia. Daniel le dijo: «No mates a los sabios de Babilonia. Llévame ante el rey. Yo le explicaré su sueño».

decisions.choice: do not destroy the wise men of Babylon: Daniel speaks for the others too
decisions.reason: Daniel's first concern is for all the wise men, not only for himself and his friends. The God who revealed the secret saves even the Babylonian experts who could not.

decisions.choice: Arioch, whom the king had appointed: the officer of verse 14
decisions.reason: Arioch carries out the king's sentence, and only he can stop it or bring Daniel before the king.

decisions.choice: put ... to death (B); kill (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12, "destroy" here means "put to death".

source.text: אֱדַ֤יִן אַרְיוֹךְ֙ בְּהִתְבְּהָלָ֔ה הַנְעֵ֥ל לְדָנִיֵּ֖אל קֳדָ֣ם מַלְכָּ֑א וְכֵ֣ן אֲמַר־לֵ֗הּ דִּֽי־הַשְׁכַּ֤חַת גְּבַר֙ מִן־בְּנֵ֤י גָֽלוּתָא֙ דִּ֣י יְה֔וּד דִּ֥י פִשְׁרָ֖א לְמַלְכָּ֥א יְהוֹדַֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Then Arioch in haste brought in Daniel before the king, and thus said to him: I have found a man from the sons of the exile of Judah who the interpretation to the king will make known.

en.L: Then Arioch brought Daniel in haste before the king and said thus to him, "I have found a man from the exiles of Judah who will make known the interpretation to the king."
en.B: Arioch quickly took Daniel to the king and said, "I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can tell the king the interpretation."
en.R: Arioch hurried to take Daniel to the king. He said, "I have found one of the captives from Judah who can explain your dream to you."

fr.L: Alors Aryok, en hâte, fit entrer Daniel devant le roi et lui dit ainsi : « J’ai trouvé un homme parmi les exilés de Juda, qui fera connaître l’interprétation au roi. »
fr.B: Aryok conduisit aussitôt Daniel auprès du roi et lui dit : « J’ai trouvé parmi les exilés de Juda un homme qui peut donner au roi l’interprétation. »
fr.R: Aryok s’est dépêché d’emmener Daniel chez le roi. Il a dit : « J’ai trouvé un des prisonniers venus de Juda qui peut t’expliquer ton rêve. »

es.L: Entonces Arioc llevó apresuradamente a Daniel delante del rey, y le dijo así: «He hallado un hombre de los desterrados de Judá que dará a conocer al rey la interpretación».
es.B: Arioc llevó enseguida a Daniel ante el rey y le dijo: «He encontrado entre los desterrados de Judá a un hombre que puede decirle al rey la interpretación».
es.R: Arioc llevó a Daniel ante el rey a toda prisa y le dijo: «He encontrado a uno de los cautivos de Judá que puede explicarte tu sueño».

decisions.choice: I have found a man: Arioch takes some credit for himself
decisions.reason: Arioch presents Daniel as his own discovery. He may hope for reward; the text does not judge him. On how this fits Daniel's request in verse 16, see the note there.

decisions.choice: the sons of the exile of Judah: the exiles from Judah
decisions.reason: "Sons of the exile" is a way of saying "exiles", the people taken from Judah to Babylon (Ezra 6:16).

decisions.choice: captives (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "captives" for "exiles" and "explain your dream to you" for the courtly "make known to the king".

decisions.choice: "los desterrados de Judá" (L, B); "los cautivos de Judá" (R)
decisions.reason: "Desterrados" is the published word for the exiles (2 Kings; Ezekiel); R says "cautivos", as the English R says "captives"

source.text: עָנֵ֤ה מַלְכָּא֙ וְאָמַ֣ר לְדָנִיֵּ֔אל דִּ֥י שְׁמֵ֖הּ בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּ֑ר הַֽאִיתָ֣ךְ כָּהֵ֗ל לְהוֹדָעֻתַ֛נִי חֶלְמָ֥א דִֽי־חֲזֵ֖ית וּפִשְׁרֵֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Answering the king and saying to Daniel whose name [was] Belteshazzar: are you able to make known to me the dream which I saw and its interpretation?

en.L: The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to declare to me the dream that I saw, and its interpretation?"
en.B: The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Can you tell me the dream I had and what it means?"
en.R: The king said to Daniel (who was also called Belteshazzar), "Can you tell me what I dreamed and what it means?"

fr.L: Le roi répondit et dit à Daniel, dont le nom était Beltshatsar : « Es-tu capable de me faire connaître le songe que j’ai vu et son interprétation ? »
fr.B: Le roi dit à Daniel, qui s’appelait Beltshatsar : « Peux-tu me dire le songe que j’ai eu et ce qu’il signifie ? »
fr.R: Le roi a dit à Daniel (qu’on appelait aussi Beltshatsar) : « Peux-tu me dire ce que j’ai rêvé et ce que cela veut dire ? »

es.L: Respondió el rey y dijo a Daniel, cuyo nombre era Beltsasar: «¿Eres tú capaz de darme a conocer el sueño que vi y su interpretación?».
es.B: El rey le dijo a Daniel, a quien llamaban Beltsasar: «¿Puedes decirme el sueño que tuve y lo que significa?».
es.R: El rey le dijo a Daniel (que también se llamaba Beltsasar): «¿Puedes decirme lo que soñé y lo que significa?».

decisions.choice: whose name was Belteshazzar: the court name of 1:7
decisions.reason: The narrator reminds the reader that the king knows Daniel by his Babylonian name.

decisions.choice: who was also called Belteshazzar (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says "also called", so that readers do not think Daniel has become another person.

source.text: עָנֵ֧ה דָנִיֵּ֛אל קֳדָ֥ם מַלְכָּ֖א וְאָמַ֑ר רָזָה֙ דִּֽי־מַלְכָּ֣א שָׁאֵ֔ל לָ֧א חַכִּימִ֣ין אָֽשְׁפִ֗ין חַרְטֻמִּין֙ גָּזְרִ֔ין יָכְלִ֖ין לְהַֽחֲוָיָ֥ה לְמַלְכָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Answering Daniel before the king and saying: the secret which the king [is] asking, not wise men, enchanters, magicians, diviners are able to declare to the king.

en.L: Daniel answered before the king and said, "The secret that the king asks, no wise men, enchanters, magicians [or] diviners are able to declare to the king.
en.B: Daniel replied to the king, "No wise men, enchanters, magicians or diviners can explain to the king the mystery he has asked about.
en.R: Daniel answered the king, "No wise men, enchanters, magicians or diviners can tell you the secret you want to know.

fr.L: Daniel répondit devant le roi et dit : « Le mystère que le roi demande, ni sages, ni enchanteurs, ni magiciens, ni devins ne peuvent l’exposer au roi.
fr.B: Daniel répondit au roi : « Ni sages, ni enchanteurs, ni magiciens, ni devins ne peuvent révéler au roi le mystère qu’il demande.
fr.R: Daniel a répondu au roi : « Aucun sage, aucun enchanteur, aucun magicien ni aucun devin ne peut te dire le secret que tu veux connaître.

es.L: Respondió Daniel delante del rey y dijo: «El misterio que el rey pregunta, ni sabios, ni encantadores, ni magos, ni adivinos lo pueden declarar al rey.
es.B: Daniel le respondió al rey: «Ni sabios, ni encantadores, ni magos, ni adivinos pueden explicarle al rey el misterio por el que ha preguntado.
es.R: Daniel le respondió al rey: «Ni los sabios, ni los encantadores, ni los magos, ni los adivinos pueden decirte el secreto que quieres saber.

decisions.choice: diviners: experts who foretold the future
decisions.reason: The word comes from a verb meaning "to cut" or "to decide", and probably names those who determined fates, perhaps by reading the stars or omens (4:4; 5:7, 11). It is used only in Daniel's lists.

decisions.choice: no wise men ... are able: human skill cannot reveal the secret
decisions.reason: Daniel agrees with the Chaldeans (verses 10-11). The secret is beyond human wisdom, and that is why the answer must come from God (verse 28).

decisions.choice: the list kept at every level: wise men, enchanters, magicians, diviners
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, each group of experts keeps its own word at every level. "Diviners" is chosen for the last, since Readable already uses "astrologers" for the Chaldeans as a class.

source.text: בְּרַ֡ם אִיתַ֞י אֱלָ֤הּ בִּשְׁמַיָּא֙ גָּלֵ֣א רָזִ֔ין וְהוֹדַ֗ע לְמַלְכָּא֙ נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֔ר מָ֛ה דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֵ֖א בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית יוֹמַיָּ֑א חֶלְמָ֨ךְ וְחֶזְוֵ֥י רֵאשָׁ֛ךְ עַֽל־מִשְׁכְּבָ֖ךְ דְּנָ֥ה הֽוּא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: However, there is a God in the heavens who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the king Nebuchadnezzar what will be in the end of the days. Your dream and the visions of your head on your bed, this [is] it:

en.L: However, there is a God in heaven, a revealer of secrets, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be at the end of the days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed, this [is] it:
en.B: But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the days to come. This was your dream, the visions that passed through your mind as you lay in bed:
en.R: But there is a God in heaven who shows people secrets. He has shown you, King Nebuchadnezzar, what is going to happen in the future. Here is the dream you had, the vision you saw while you were lying in bed.

fr.L: Mais il y a un Dieu dans les cieux qui révèle les mystères, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a fait connaître au roi Nabuchodonosor ce qui arrivera à la fin des jours. Ton songe et les visions de ta tête sur ta couche, les voici :
fr.B: Mais il y a dans les cieux un Dieu qui révèle les mystères. Il a fait connaître au roi Nabuchodonosor ce qui arrivera dans les jours à venir. Voici ton songe, les visions qui ont traversé ton esprit pendant que tu étais couché :
fr.R: Mais il y a dans le ciel un Dieu qui fait connaître les secrets aux gens. Il t’a montré, roi Nabuchodonosor, ce qui va arriver dans l’avenir. Voici le rêve que tu as fait, la vision que tu as eue pendant que tu étais couché.

es.L: Pero hay un Dios en los cielos que revela los misterios, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha hecho saber al rey Nabucodonosor lo que ha de suceder al final de los días. Tu sueño y las visiones de tu cabeza sobre tu cama, esto [es]:
es.B: Pero hay un Dios en los cielos que revela los misterios. Él le ha mostrado al rey Nabucodonosor lo que sucederá en los días venideros. Este fue tu sueño, las visiones que pasaron por tu mente mientras estabas acostado:
es.R: Pero hay un Dios en el cielo que da a conocer los secretos. Él te ha mostrado a ti, rey Nabucodonosor, lo que va a pasar en el futuro. Este es el sueño que tuviste, la visión que viste mientras estabas acostado en tu cama.

decisions.choice: at the end of the days: in the time to come
decisions.reason: The phrase means the future, sometimes the far future when God's purposes are fulfilled (Genesis 49:1; Isaiah 2:2; Daniel 10:14). Here it covers the kingdoms of the dream down to the kingdom God will set up (verse 44). It does not by itself mean the end of the world.

decisions.choice: the visions of your head: what you saw in your mind
decisions.reason: In Aramaic the head is where one sees in dreams and thoughts (4:2, 7, 10; 7:1, 15).

decisions.choice: there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets
decisions.reason: Daniel answers the Chaldeans' claim that only gods far from mortals could do this (verse 11): there is such a God, and he reveals. The phrase "revealer of secrets" returns in the king's confession (verse 47).

decisions.choice: visions that passed through your mind (B); the vision you saw (R)
decisions.reason: "The visions of your head" is an Aramaic idiom (m2); Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: אַ֣נְתְּהמַלְכָּ֗א רַעְיוֹנָךְ֙ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבָ֣ךְ סְלִ֔קוּ מָ֛ה דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֵ֖א אַחֲרֵ֣י דְנָ֑ה וְגָלֵ֧א רָזַיָּ֛א הוֹדְעָ֖ךְ מָה־דִ֥י לֶהֱוֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: You, O king, your thoughts on your bed came up [about] what will be after this, and the revealer of secrets has made known to you what will be.

en.L: You, O king, your thoughts came up on your bed [about] what would be after this, and the revealer of secrets has made known to you what will be.
en.B: As you lay in bed, O king, your thoughts turned to what would happen in the future, and the revealer of mysteries has shown you what is going to happen.
en.R: Your Majesty, while you were lying in bed, you began to think about the future. And God, who shows people secrets, has shown you what will happen.

fr.L: Toi, ô roi, tes pensées sont montées sur ta couche [au sujet de] ce qui arriverait après cela, et celui qui révèle les mystères t’a fait connaître ce qui arrivera.
fr.B: Pendant que tu étais couché, ô roi, tes pensées se sont tournées vers ce qui arriverait dans l’avenir, et celui qui révèle les mystères t’a montré ce qui va arriver.
fr.R: Ô roi, pendant que tu étais couché, tu t’es mis à penser à l’avenir. Et Dieu, qui fait connaître les secrets aux gens, t’a montré ce qui va arriver.

es.L: Tú, oh rey, tus pensamientos subieron sobre tu cama [acerca de] lo que sucedería después de esto, y el que revela los misterios te ha dado a conocer lo que ha de ser.
es.B: Estando en tu cama, oh rey, tus pensamientos se dirigieron a lo que sucedería en el futuro, y el que revela los misterios te ha mostrado lo que va a suceder.
es.R: Mi rey, mientras estabas acostado en tu cama, comenzaste a pensar en el futuro. Y Dios, que da a conocer los secretos, te ha mostrado lo que va a pasar.

decisions.choice: your thoughts came up about what would be after this
decisions.reason: Daniel suggests that the dream answered the king's own thoughts as he lay awake wondering about the future of his kingdom.

decisions.choice: the revealer of secrets: God
decisions.reason: Daniel names God by what he does, as in verse 28. He takes no credit for himself (verse 30).

decisions.choice: God, who shows people secrets (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God for "the revealer of secrets", which is what the title refers to.

source.text: וַאֲנָ֗ה לָ֤א בְחָכְמָה֙ דִּֽי־אִיתַ֥י בִּי֙ מִן־כָּל־חַיַּיָּ֔א רָזָ֥א דְנָ֖ה גֱּלִ֣י לִ֑י לָהֵ֗ן עַל־דִּבְרַת֙ דִּ֤י פִשְׁרָא֙ לְמַלְכָּ֣א יְהוֹדְע֔וּן וְרַעְיוֹנֵ֥י לִבְבָ֖ךְ תִּנְדַּֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, not by wisdom that is in me more than all the living has this secret been revealed to me, but for the sake that the interpretation to the king they may make known, and the thoughts of your heart you may know.

en.L: And as for me, not by wisdom that is in me more than [in] all the living has this secret been revealed to me, but so that they may make known the interpretation to the king, and [so that] you may know the thoughts of your heart.
en.B: As for me, this mystery has not been revealed to me because I have more wisdom than anyone else alive, but so that the king may know the interpretation and understand the thoughts of his heart.
en.R: God did not show me this secret because I am wiser than other people. He showed it to me so that you could know what the dream means, Your Majesty, and understand what you were thinking about.

fr.L: Et quant à moi, ce n’est pas par une sagesse qui serait en moi plus qu’en tous les vivants que ce mystère m’a été révélé, mais afin qu’on fasse connaître l’interprétation au roi, et [afin] que tu connaisses les pensées de ton cœur.
fr.B: Quant à moi, si ce mystère m’a été révélé, ce n’est pas que j’aie plus de sagesse que tous les autres vivants, mais c’est pour que le roi en connaisse l’interprétation et comprenne les pensées de son cœur.
fr.R: Dieu ne m’a pas montré ce secret parce que je suis plus sage que les autres. Il me l’a montré pour que tu saches, ô roi, ce que veut dire ton rêve, et pour que tu comprennes à quoi tu pensais.

es.L: Y en cuanto a mí, no por sabiduría que haya en mí más que [en] todos los vivientes me ha sido revelado este misterio, sino para que se dé a conocer al rey la interpretación, y [para que] tú conozcas los pensamientos de tu corazón.
es.B: En cuanto a mí, este misterio no se me ha revelado porque yo tenga más sabiduría que cualquier otro ser viviente, sino para que el rey conozca la interpretación y entienda los pensamientos de su corazón.
es.R: Dios no me mostró este secreto porque yo sea más sabio que los demás. Me lo mostró para que tú, mi rey, sepas lo que significa el sueño y entiendas lo que estabas pensando.

decisions.choice: not by wisdom that is in me: the revelation is God's gift, not Daniel's skill
decisions.reason: Daniel sets aside any claim to superior wisdom, as Joseph did before Pharaoh (Genesis 41:16).

decisions.choice: they may make known: the interpretation may be made known
decisions.reason: The Aramaic says "they will make known" with no stated subject. This is a common Aramaic way of saying a passive ("it will be made known"), and it may hint at God and his heavenly servants as the ones who make it known (compare 4:13-14).

decisions.choice: God did not show me (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who revealed the secret, which verses 28-29 make plain.

source.text: אַ֣נְתְּהמַלְכָּ֗א חָזֵ֤ה הֲוַ֨יְתָ֙ וַאֲל֨וּ צְלֵ֥ם חַד֙ שַׂגִּ֔יא צַלְמָ֨א דִּכֵּ֥ן רַ֛ב וְזִיוֵ֥הּ יַתִּ֖יר קָאֵ֣ם לְקָבְלָ֑ךְ וְרֵוֵ֖הּ דְּחִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: You, O king, were seeing, and look, an image, one great. This image [was] mighty, and its brightness [was] extraordinary; standing before you, and its appearance [was] terrifying.

en.L: You, O king, were looking, and there was one great image. This image was mighty, and its brightness was extraordinary; it stood before you, and its appearance was terrifying.
en.B: You were watching, O king, and there before you stood a great statue. This statue was huge and its brightness dazzling, and it stood in front of you, frightening to look at.
en.R: Your Majesty, in your dream you saw a huge statue standing in front of you. It was very bright and shining, and it was terrifying to look at.

fr.L: Toi, ô roi, tu regardais, et voici une grande statue. Cette statue était puissante, et son éclat extraordinaire ; elle se tenait devant toi, et son aspect était terrifiant.
fr.B: Tu regardais, ô roi, et voici qu’une grande statue se dressait devant toi. Cette statue était immense et d’un éclat éblouissant ; elle se tenait face à toi, et elle était effrayante à voir.
fr.R: Ô roi, dans ton rêve, tu as vu une statue immense debout devant toi. Elle était très brillante et elle faisait peur à voir.

es.L: Tú, oh rey, estabas mirando, y he aquí una gran imagen. Esta imagen era enorme, y su resplandor extraordinario; estaba en pie delante de ti, y su aspecto era terrible.
es.B: Tú, oh rey, estabas mirando, y delante de ti se alzaba una gran estatua. Era una estatua enorme y de un brillo deslumbrante; estaba de pie frente a ti, y daba miedo mirarla.
es.R: Mi rey, en tu sueño viste una estatua enorme que estaba de pie delante de ti. Era muy brillante y resplandeciente, y daba terror mirarla.

decisions.choice: an image: a statue in human form
