decisions.reason: The word *tselem* means an image or likeness, here a statue of a man (verse 32). It is the word used for the gold image in chapter 3.

decisions.choice: and behold: and there was
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word points to something seen suddenly, like the Hebrew word often rendered "behold".

decisions.choice: statue (B, R); image (L); there was (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "image", the word that links this dream with chapter 3. Balanced and Readable say "statue", which is what the image is. "Behold" is not used (m2).

decisions.choice: "statue" at every level for tselem, here and in chapter 3
decisions.reason: French "image" today means a picture, not a carved figure; "statue" is the plain word for a figure in human form, at Literal too, where the English keeps "image".

decisions.choice: "imagen" (L); "estatua" (B, R)
decisions.reason: A statue in human form; L keeps "imagen" as in chapter 3 ("la imagen de oro" L, "la estatua de oro" B, R)

source.text: ה֣וּא צַלְמָ֗א רֵאשֵׁהּ֙ דִּֽי־דְהַ֣ב טָ֔ב חֲד֥וֹהִי וּדְרָע֖וֹהִי דִּ֣י כְסַ֑ף מְע֥וֹהִי וְיַרְכָתֵ֖הּ דִּ֥י נְחָֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: That image, its head [was] of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,

en.L: That image: its head [was] of fine gold, its chest and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of bronze,
en.B: The head of the statue was made of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,
en.R: The statue's head was made of pure gold. Its chest and arms were made of silver. Its belly and thighs were made of bronze.

fr.L: Cette statue : sa tête [était] d’or fin, sa poitrine et ses bras d’argent, son ventre et ses cuisses de bronze,
fr.B: La tête de la statue était d’or fin, sa poitrine et ses bras d’argent, son ventre et ses cuisses de bronze,
fr.R: La tête de la statue était en or pur. Sa poitrine et ses bras étaient en argent. Son ventre et ses cuisses étaient en bronze.

es.L: La cabeza de esta imagen [era] de oro fino; su pecho y sus brazos, de plata; su vientre y sus muslos, de bronce;
es.B: La cabeza de la estatua era de oro fino; el pecho y los brazos, de plata; el vientre y los muslos, de bronce;
es.R: La cabeza de la estatua era de oro puro. El pecho y los brazos eran de plata. El vientre y los muslos eran de bronce.

decisions.choice: gold, silver, bronze, iron: metals of decreasing value
decisions.reason: The metals go down in value from head to foot, while growing in hardness, until the feet of iron and clay (verses 33, 41-43). The order prepares for the interpretation in verses 38-43.

decisions.choice: a comma at the end (L, B)
decisions.reason: The description runs on into verse 33, so Literal and Balanced end the verse with a comma. Readable makes each part a sentence.

source.text: שָׁק֖וֹהִי דִּ֣י פַרְזֶ֑ל רַגְל֕וֹהִי מִנְּהֵין֙ דִּ֣י פַרְזֶ֔ל וּמִנְּהֵ֖ין דִּ֥י חֲסַֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.

en.L: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.
en.B: its legs of iron, and its feet partly of iron and partly of baked clay.
en.R: Its legs were made of iron. Its feet were partly iron and partly clay.

fr.L: ses jambes de fer, ses pieds en partie de fer et en partie d’argile.
fr.B: ses jambes de fer, et ses pieds en partie de fer et en partie d’argile cuite.
fr.R: Ses jambes étaient en fer. Ses pieds étaient en partie en fer et en partie en argile.

es.L: sus piernas, de hierro; sus pies, en parte de hierro y en parte de barro.
es.B: las piernas, de hierro; y los pies, en parte de hierro y en parte de barro cocido.
es.R: Las piernas eran de hierro, y los pies eran en parte de hierro y en parte de barro.

decisions.choice: clay: baked clay, as in pottery
decisions.reason: The word means potter's clay (verse 41, "potter's clay"), probably fired, so that it would break when struck (verse 42). Iron and clay do not bond, which is the point of verse 43.

decisions.choice: baked clay (B)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "baked" from verse 41, where it is "potter's clay", to show that it is brittle.

source.text: חָזֵ֣ה הֲוַ֗יְתָ עַ֠ד דִּ֣י הִתְגְּזֶ֤רֶת אֶ֨בֶן֙ דִּי־לָ֣א בִידַ֔יִן וּמְחָ֤ת לְצַלְמָא֙ עַל־רַגְל֔וֹהִי דִּ֥י פַרְזְלָ֖א וְחַסְפָּ֑א וְהַדֵּ֖קֶת הִמּֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Seeing you were until that a stone was cut out which [was] not by hands, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay, and shattered them.

en.L: You were looking until a stone was cut out, not by hands, and it struck the image on its feet of iron and clay and shattered them.
en.B: While you watched, a stone was cut out, though no human hand touched it. It struck the statue's feet of iron and clay and smashed them.
en.R: As you watched, a rock was cut from a mountain, but no human hand cut it. The rock hit the feet of the statue, which were made of iron and clay, and smashed them to pieces.

fr.L: Tu regardais, jusqu’à ce qu’une pierre se détacha, non par des mains, et elle frappa la statue sur ses pieds de fer et d’argile, et les brisa.
fr.B: Tandis que tu regardais, une pierre se détacha sans qu’aucune main humaine y touche. Elle frappa les pieds de fer et d’argile de la statue et les mit en pièces.
fr.R: Pendant que tu regardais, un rocher s’est détaché d’une montagne, mais aucune main humaine ne l’avait détaché. Le rocher a frappé les pieds de la statue, qui étaient en fer et en argile, et les a brisés en morceaux.

es.L: Estabas mirando, hasta que una piedra fue cortada, no con manos, e hirió a la imagen en sus pies de hierro y de barro, y los desmenuzó.
es.B: Mientras mirabas, se desprendió una piedra sin que mano humana la tocara. Golpeó a la estatua en los pies de hierro y de barro, y los hizo pedazos.
es.R: Mientras mirabas, una roca se desprendió de una montaña, pero ninguna mano humana la cortó. La roca golpeó los pies de la estatua, que eran de hierro y de barro, y los hizo pedazos.

decisions.choice: not by hands: by no human power
decisions.reason: "Not made with hands" means made by God (compare 8:25; Job 34:20; Lamentations 4:6). The stone is cut by God himself, and it stands for the kingdom he will set up (verses 44-45).

decisions.choice: a stone: a picture of God's kingdom
decisions.reason: Verse 45 adds that the stone was cut from a mountain. The image of a stone recalls other passages about God's work (Isaiah 28:16; Psalm 118:22), and Jesus speaks of the stone that crushes those it falls on (Luke 20:17-18), which many readers link with this dream. The dream itself says only that the stone stands for God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: a rock was cut from a mountain (R)
decisions.reason: Readable brings in the mountain from verse 45, so that young readers can picture where the stone came from, and says "rock" for a stone of this size.

source.text: בֵּאדַ֣יִן דָּ֣קוּ כַחֲדָ֡ה פַּרְזְלָא֩ חַסְפָּ֨א נְחָשָׁ֜א כַּסְפָּ֣א וְדַהֲבָ֗א וַהֲווֹ֙ כְּע֣וּר מִן־אִדְּרֵי־קַ֔יִט וּנְשָׂ֤א הִמּוֹן֙ רוּחָ֔א וְכָל־אֲתַ֖ר לָא־הִשְׁתֲּכַ֣ח לְה֑וֹן וְאַבְנָ֣א׀דִּֽי־מְחָ֣ת לְצַלְמָ֗א הֲוָ֛ת לְט֥וּר רַ֖ב וּמְלָ֥ת כָּל־אַרְעָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Then were shattered together the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold, and they became like chaff from threshing floors of summer, and carried them away the wind, and any place not was found for them; and the stone that struck the image became a mountain great and filled all the earth.

en.L: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were shattered together, and they became like chaff from the summer threshing floors; and the wind carried them away, and no trace of them was found. And the stone that struck the image became a great mountain, and it filled all the earth.
en.B: Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were all broken to pieces at once and became like chaff on a threshing floor in summer. The wind swept them away, and not a trace of them remained. But the stone that had struck the statue grew into a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
en.R: Then all of it, the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold, broke to pieces at the same time. It became like the husks that blow away when farmers separate the grain in summer. The wind blew the pieces away until nothing was left. But the rock that hit the statue grew into a huge mountain that covered the whole earth.

fr.L: Alors furent brisés ensemble le fer, l’argile, le bronze, l’argent et l’or, et ils devinrent comme la balle des aires en été ; et le vent les emporta, et on n’en trouva plus aucune trace. Et la pierre qui avait frappé la statue devint une grande montagne, et elle remplit toute la terre.
fr.B: Alors le fer, l’argile, le bronze, l’argent et l’or furent tous brisés d’un coup et devinrent comme la balle sur l’aire en été. Le vent les emporta, et il n’en resta pas la moindre trace. Mais la pierre qui avait frappé la statue devint une grande montagne et remplit toute la terre.
fr.R: Alors tout s’est brisé en morceaux en même temps : le fer, l’argile, le bronze, l’argent et l’or. C’est devenu comme les petites peaux des grains de blé qui s’envolent quand on sépare le grain en été. Le vent a emporté les morceaux, et il n’est plus rien resté. Mais le rocher qui avait frappé la statue est devenu une énorme montagne qui a couvert toute la terre.

es.L: Entonces fueron desmenuzados juntamente el hierro, el barro, el bronce, la plata y el oro, y quedaron como el tamo de las eras en verano; y se los llevó el viento, y no se halló lugar para ellos. Y la piedra que hirió a la imagen se hizo un gran monte, y llenó toda la tierra.
es.B: Entonces el hierro, el barro, el bronce, la plata y el oro se hicieron pedazos al mismo tiempo, y quedaron como la paja de las eras en verano. El viento se los llevó, y no quedó rastro de ellos. Pero la piedra que había golpeado a la estatua se convirtió en una gran montaña y llenó toda la tierra.
es.R: Entonces todo, el hierro, el barro, el bronce, la plata y el oro, se hizo pedazos al mismo tiempo. Quedó como la cáscara del grano que se lleva el viento cuando los campesinos limpian el trigo en verano. El viento se llevó los pedazos hasta que no quedó nada. Pero la roca que golpeó a la estatua creció hasta ser una montaña enorme que cubrió toda la tierra.

decisions.choice: chaff from the summer threshing floors
decisions.reason: At harvest, grain was beaten on an open threshing floor and tossed in the wind, which carried off the light husks, the chaff. Chaff blown away by the wind is a common picture of the wicked or of enemies swept away (Psalm 1:4; Isaiah 41:15-16; Hosea 13:3).

decisions.choice: no place was found for them: they vanished completely
decisions.reason: The words mean that not a trace was left (compare Revelation 20:11).

decisions.choice: became a great mountain and filled the whole earth
decisions.reason: A mountain is a picture of a kingdom, and God's mountain of his reign over the world (Isaiah 2:2; 11:9). The kingdom that the stone stands for grows to fill the earth (verse 44).

decisions.choice: the husks that blow away when farmers separate the grain in summer (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what chaff and threshing floors are (m1).

source.text: דְּנָ֣ה חֶלְמָ֔א וּפִשְׁרֵ֖הּ נֵאמַ֥ר קֳדָם־מַלְכָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: This [was] the dream, and its interpretation we will tell before the king.

en.L: This [was] the dream, and we will tell its interpretation before the king.
en.B: That was the dream. Now we will tell the king its interpretation.
en.R: That was your dream. Now we will tell you what it means.

fr.L: Tel [était] le songe, et nous en dirons l’interprétation devant le roi.
fr.B: Tel était le songe. Maintenant, nous allons en donner l’interprétation au roi.
fr.R: Voilà ton rêve. Maintenant, nous allons te dire ce qu’il veut dire.

es.L: Este [es] el sueño, y su interpretación la diremos delante del rey.
es.B: Ese fue el sueño. Ahora le diremos al rey su interpretación.
es.R: Ese fue tu sueño. Ahora te diremos lo que significa.

decisions.choice: we will tell: Daniel speaks for his friends as well, or as the king's servant
decisions.reason: Daniel says "we". He may include his three friends, who prayed with him (verses 17-18, 23), or speak in a modest way of himself.

decisions.choice: tell you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the king directly, as in verse 29.

source.text: אַ֣נְתְּהמַלְכָּ֔א מֶ֖לֶךְ מַלְכַיָּ֑א דִּ֚י אֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א מַלְכוּתָ֥א חִסְנָ֛א וְתָקְפָּ֥א וִֽיקָרָ֖א יְהַב־לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: You, O king, [are] king of the kings, to whom the God of the heavens the kingdom, the power and the strength and the honor has given to you,

en.L: You, O king, [are] king of the kings, to whom the God of heaven has granted the kingdom, the power and the strength and the honor,
en.B: You, O king, are the king of kings. The God of heaven has given you the kingdom, the power, the might and the glory.
en.R: Your Majesty, you are the greatest of all kings. The God of heaven has given you your kingdom, your power, your strength and your honor.

fr.L: Toi, ô roi, [tu es] le roi des rois, à qui le Dieu des cieux a donné le royaume, la puissance, la force et l’honneur,
fr.B: Toi, ô roi, tu es le roi des rois. Le Dieu des cieux t’a donné le royaume, la puissance, la force et la gloire.
fr.R: Ô roi, tu es le plus grand de tous les rois. Le Dieu du ciel t’a donné ton royaume, ta puissance, ta force et ton honneur.

es.L: Tú, oh rey, [eres] rey de reyes, a quien el Dios de los cielos ha dado el reino, el poder, la fuerza y la honra,
es.B: Tú, oh rey, eres el rey de reyes. El Dios de los cielos te ha dado el reino, el poder, la fuerza y la gloria.
es.R: Mi rey, tú eres el más grande de todos los reyes. El Dios de los cielos te ha dado tu reino, tu poder, tu fuerza y tu honor.

decisions.choice: king of kings: the greatest of kings, ruling over other kings
decisions.reason: This was a title of the kings of Babylon and Persia (Ezra 7:12; Ezekiel 26:7), who ruled over lesser kings. Daniel uses it, but at once says that Nebuchadnezzar's rule was given by God.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven has given you the kingdom
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar did not win his empire by his own power; it was given by God (Jeremiah 27:5-7). This is the lesson he must learn in chapter 4 (4:22, 29; 5:18-21).

decisions.choice: honor (L, R); glory (B)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word means honor or splendor. Literal and Readable say "honor", Balanced "glory". The sentence runs on into verse 38 at Literal; Balanced and Readable end it here.

source.text: וּבְכָל־דִּ֣י דָֽיְרִ֣ין בְּֽנֵי־אֲ֠נָשָׁא חֵיוַ֨ת בָּרָ֤א וְעוֹף־שְׁמַיָּא֙ יְהַ֣ב בִּידָ֔ךְ וְהַשְׁלְטָ֖ךְ בְּכָלְּה֑וֹן אַנְתְּה־ה֔וּארֵאשָׁ֖ה דִּ֥י דַהֲבָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And in all where dwell the sons of mankind, the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens, he has given into your hand and has made you ruler over all of them. You [are] it, the head of gold.

en.L: and wherever the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}} dwell, the animals of the field and the birds of the heavens {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given into your hand, and made you rule over all of them. You are the head of gold.
en.B: Wherever people live, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has put them in your power, and the wild animals and the birds of the sky too, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.
en.R: God has put you in charge of all people everywhere. He has also put you in charge of the wild animals and the birds. He has made you ruler over all of them. You are the head of gold.

fr.L: et partout où habitent les {{gender:enfants des humains|fils des hommes}}, les bêtes des champs et les oiseaux des cieux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a livrés en ta main, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’a fait dominer sur eux tous. C’est toi qui es la tête d’or.
fr.B: Partout où vivent les humains, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a mis en ton pouvoir, avec les bêtes sauvages et les oiseaux du ciel, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} t’a fait régner sur eux tous. C’est toi qui es la tête d’or.
fr.R: Dieu t’a donné le pouvoir sur tous les gens, partout. Il t’a aussi donné le pouvoir sur les animaux sauvages et sur les oiseaux. Il t’a fait roi sur eux tous. C’est toi, la tête d’or.

es.L: y dondequiera que habitan los hijos de los hombres, las bestias del campo y las aves de los cielos, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los ha entregado en tu mano, y te ha hecho señor sobre todos ellos. Tú eres la cabeza de oro.
es.B: Dondequiera que vive la gente, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} la ha puesto bajo tu poder, y también a los animales salvajes y a las aves del cielo, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} te ha hecho gobernante de todos ellos. Tú eres la cabeza de oro.
es.R: Dios te ha puesto al mando de toda la gente, en todas partes. También te ha puesto al mando de los animales salvajes y de las aves. Te ha hecho gobernante de todos ellos. Tú eres la cabeza de oro.

decisions.choice: wherever the sons of men dwell: all people, and the animals too
decisions.reason: The Aramaic is compressed: "in all where dwell the sons of men, the beasts of the field and the birds of the heavens". It most likely means that God has given into the king's power all people, wherever they live, and the animals as well. The words recall the rule given to humankind in Genesis 1:28 and the beasts that serve Nebuchadnezzar in Jeremiah 27:6; 28:14.

decisions.choice: you are the head of gold: Nebuchadnezzar and his kingdom
decisions.reason: Daniel names the first kingdom: the king himself, standing for the Babylonian empire. The next kingdoms are not named in this chapter (see verse 39).

decisions.choice: the sons of men (L); people (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic phrase means human beings as a whole, men and women. Literal gives it as "children of humankind", with "sons of men" as the gender setting's alternative; Balanced and Readable say "people".

decisions.choice: "los hijos de los hombres"
decisions.reason: The Spanish phrase already includes women and men, so it takes no gender span where the English has one

source.text: וּבָתְרָ֗ךְ תְּק֛וּם מַלְכ֥וּ אָחֳרִ֖י אֲרַעמִנָּ֑ךְ וּמַלְכ֨וּ תְלִיתָאָ֤ה אָחֳרִי֙ דִּ֣י נְחָשָׁ֔א דִּ֥י תִשְׁלַ֖ט בְּכָל־אַרְעָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And after you will arise a kingdom another, lower than you, and a kingdom third another, of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.

en.L: And after you will arise another kingdom, lower than you, and another, a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
en.B: After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours, and then a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over the whole earth.
en.R: After your kingdom ends, another kingdom will come. It will not be as great as yours. Then a third kingdom, the bronze one, will rule over the whole earth.

fr.L: Et après toi s’élèvera un autre royaume, inférieur à toi, et un autre, un troisième royaume, de bronze, qui dominera sur toute la terre.
fr.B: Après toi s’élèvera un autre royaume, inférieur au tien, puis un troisième royaume, de bronze, qui dominera sur toute la terre.
fr.R: Quand ton royaume aura pris fin, un autre royaume viendra. Il ne sera pas aussi grand que le tien. Ensuite, un troisième royaume, celui de bronze, dominera toute la terre.

es.L: Y después de ti se levantará otro reino, inferior a ti, y otro tercer reino, de bronce, que dominará sobre toda la tierra.
es.B: Después de ti surgirá otro reino, inferior al tuyo, y luego un tercer reino, de bronce, que gobernará sobre toda la tierra.
es.R: Cuando tu reino termine, vendrá otro reino que no será tan grande como el tuyo. Después, un tercer reino, el de bronce, gobernará sobre toda la tierra.

decisions.choice: the second and third kingdoms: not named in the dream
decisions.reason: The dream does not name the kingdoms after Babylon. Most readers take the four kingdoms of this chapter to be the same as the four beasts of chapter 7. Two main readings are held: (1) Babylon, Media, Persia and Greece (the empire of Alexander and the kingdoms that followed it), which fits the book's own order, with Darius the Mede before Cyrus the Persian (6:1, 29); (2) Babylon, Media-Persia, Greece and Rome, the reading of many Christian and Jewish interpreters from early times. Chapter 8 names Media and Persia, and Greece, as kingdoms after Babylon (8:20-21). The text here settles none of this.

decisions.choice: lower than you: inferior to you
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word means "toward the earth", that is, lower. It may mean less in power, or less in splendor, as silver is less than gold.

decisions.choice: After your kingdom ends (R)
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that "after you" means after the king's kingdom, as verse 38 has said that he stands for it.

source.text: וּמַלְכוּ֙ רְבִ֣יעָאָ֔ה תֶּהֱוֵ֥א תַקִּיפָ֖ה כְּפַרְזְלָ֑א כָּל־קֳבֵ֗ל דִּ֤י פַרְזְלָא֙ מְהַדֵּ֤ק וְחָשֵׁל֙ כֹּ֔לָּא וּֽכְפַרְזְלָ֛א דִּֽי־מְרָעַ֥ע כָּל־אִלֵּ֖ין תַּדִּ֥ק וְתֵרֹֽעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And a kingdom fourth will be strong as the iron, because that the iron shatters and crushes everything, and as the iron that breaks, all these it will shatter and break.

en.L: And a fourth kingdom will be strong as iron, because iron shatters and crushes everything; and like iron that breaks [things], it will shatter and break all these.
en.B: Then there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron. Just as iron shatters and crushes everything, and as iron breaks things to pieces, it will crush and break all the others.
en.R: Then there will be a fourth kingdom. It will be as strong as iron. Iron breaks and smashes everything. In the same way, this kingdom will break and smash all the other kingdoms.

fr.L: Et un quatrième royaume sera fort comme le fer, parce que le fer brise et écrase tout ; et comme le fer qui broie, il brisera et broiera tous ceux-là.
fr.B: Puis il y aura un quatrième royaume, fort comme le fer. Comme le fer brise et écrase tout, comme le fer met tout en pièces, il écrasera et brisera tous les autres.
fr.R: Ensuite, il y aura un quatrième royaume. Il sera aussi fort que le fer. Le fer casse et écrase tout. De la même façon, ce royaume cassera et écrasera tous les autres royaumes.

es.L: Y el cuarto reino será fuerte como el hierro, porque el hierro desmenuza y tritura todo; y como el hierro que quebranta, desmenuzará y quebrantará todos estos.
es.B: Luego habrá un cuarto reino, fuerte como el hierro. Así como el hierro desmenuza y tritura todo, y así como el hierro lo rompe todo en pedazos, ese reino aplastará y quebrantará a todos los demás.
es.R: Después habrá un cuarto reino, tan fuerte como el hierro. El hierro rompe y destroza todo. De la misma manera, este reino romperá y destrozará a todos los otros reinos.

decisions.choice: all these: the earlier kingdoms
decisions.reason: "All these" most naturally means the kingdoms of gold, silver and bronze, which the fourth kingdom will crush. It could also mean all the things that iron breaks.

decisions.choice: the fourth kingdom: on its identity see verse 39
decisions.reason: On the identity of the fourth kingdom, see the note at verse 39.

decisions.choice: all the others (B); all the other kingdoms (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that "all these" are the earlier kingdoms (m1).

source.text: וְדִֽי־חֲזַ֜יְתָה רַגְלַיָּ֣א וְאֶצְבְּעָתָ֗א מִנְּהֵ֞ןחֲסַ֤ף דִּֽי־פֶחָר֙ וּמִנְּהֵ֣ין פַּרְזֶ֔ל מַלְכ֤וּ פְלִיגָה֙ תֶּהֱוֵ֔ה וּמִן־נִצְבְּתָ֥א דִ֥י פַרְזְלָ֖א לֶֽהֱוֵא־בַ֑הּ כָּל־קֳבֵל֙ דִּ֣י חֲזַ֔יְתָה פַּ֨רְזְלָ֔א מְעָרַ֖ב בַּחֲסַ֥ף טִינָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And that you saw the feet and the toes, partly clay of a potter and partly iron, a kingdom divided it will be, and some of the firmness of the iron will be in it, because that you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud.

en.L: And as you saw the feet and the toes, partly of potter's clay and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom; but some of the firmness of the iron will be in it, inasmuch as you saw the iron mixed with clay of mud.
en.B: And just as you saw that the feet and toes were partly potter's clay and partly iron, so it will be a divided kingdom. It will still have some of the strength of iron, as you saw iron mixed with clay.
en.R: You saw that the feet and toes were partly clay and partly iron. This means that the fourth kingdom will be divided. It will have some of the strength of iron in it, because you saw iron mixed with clay.

fr.L: Et comme tu as vu les pieds et les orteils, en partie d’argile de potier et en partie de fer, ce sera un royaume divisé ; mais il y aura en lui quelque chose de la fermeté du fer, puisque tu as vu le fer mêlé à l’argile de boue.
fr.B: Tu as vu que les pieds et les orteils étaient en partie d’argile de potier et en partie de fer : de même, ce sera un royaume divisé. Il gardera pourtant quelque chose de la solidité du fer, puisque tu as vu le fer mêlé à l’argile.
fr.R: Tu as vu que les pieds et les orteils étaient en partie en argile et en partie en fer. Cela veut dire que le quatrième royaume sera divisé. Il aura en lui un peu de la force du fer, parce que tu as vu du fer mélangé à de l’argile.

es.L: Y lo que viste de los pies y los dedos, en parte de barro de alfarero y en parte de hierro, será un reino dividido; pero habrá en él algo de la firmeza del hierro, así como viste el hierro mezclado con el barro cenagoso.
es.B: Y así como viste que los pies y los dedos eran en parte de barro de alfarero y en parte de hierro, así será un reino dividido. Aún tendrá algo de la fuerza del hierro, tal como viste el hierro mezclado con el barro.
es.R: Viste que los pies y los dedos eran en parte de barro y en parte de hierro. Eso significa que el cuarto reino estará dividido. Tendrá algo de la fuerza del hierro, porque viste hierro mezclado con barro.

decisions.choice: a divided kingdom: a kingdom made of parts that do not hold together
decisions.reason: "Divided" may mean split into parts, or made of mixed elements. Verses 42-43 explain: it will be partly strong and partly weak, and its parts will not hold together.

decisions.choice: the clay of mud: soft, wet clay
decisions.reason: Two words for clay stand together here: potter's clay and mud. The phrase stresses how soft and weak the clay is beside the iron.

decisions.choice: just as ... so (B); This means that (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that the picture is being explained, as the Aramaic "and as you saw ..." means.

source.text: וְאֶצְבְּעָת֙ רַגְלַיָּ֔א מִנְּהֵ֥ין פַּרְזֶ֖ל וּמִנְּהֵ֣ין חֲסַ֑ף מִן־קְצָ֤ת מַלְכוּתָא֙ תֶּהֱוֵ֣ה תַקִּיפָ֔ה וּמִנַּ֖הּ תֶּהֱוֵ֥ה תְבִירָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the toes of the feet, partly iron and partly clay, part of the kingdom will be strong, and part of it will be brittle.

en.L: And the toes of the feet, part of them iron and part of them clay: part of the kingdom will be strong, and part of it will be brittle.
en.B: The toes of the feet were part iron and part clay; so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
en.R: The toes were partly iron and partly clay. In the same way, part of the kingdom will be strong and part of it will be weak and easily broken.

fr.L: Et les orteils des pieds, en partie de fer et en partie d’argile : une partie du royaume sera forte, et une partie sera fragile.
fr.B: Les orteils des pieds étaient en partie de fer et en partie d’argile ; de même, le royaume sera en partie fort et en partie fragile.
fr.R: Les orteils étaient en partie en fer et en partie en argile. De la même façon, une partie du royaume sera forte, et une autre partie sera faible et facile à casser.

es.L: Y los dedos de los pies, en parte de hierro y en parte de barro: en parte el reino será fuerte, y en parte será frágil.
es.B: Los dedos de los pies eran en parte de hierro y en parte de barro; así el reino será en parte fuerte y en parte frágil.
es.R: Los dedos eran en parte de hierro y en parte de barro. De la misma manera, una parte del reino será fuerte y otra parte será débil y se romperá con facilidad.

decisions.choice: brittle: fragile, easily broken
decisions.reason: The word means breakable. Like baked clay, part of the kingdom will shatter when struck.

decisions.choice: weak and easily broken (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "brittle" in plain words.

source.text: וְדִ֣י חֲזַ֗יְתָ פַּרְזְלָא֙ מְעָרַב֙ בַּחֲסַ֣ף טִינָ֔א מִתְעָרְבִ֤ין לֶהֱוֺן֙ בִּזְרַ֣ע אֲנָשָׁ֔א וְלָֽא־לֶהֱוֺ֥ן דָּבְקִ֖ין דְּנָ֣ה עִם־דְּנָ֑ה הֵֽא־כְדִ֣י פַרְזְלָ֔א לָ֥א מִתְעָרַ֖ב עִם־חַסְפָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And that you saw the iron mixed with the clay of mud, mixing they will be with the seed of mankind, and not will they be clinging this with this, just as the iron does not mix with the clay.

en.L: And as you saw the iron mixed with clay of mud, they will be mixed by the seed of humankind, but they will not cling to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay.
en.B: And as you saw iron mixed with clay, so they will mix with one another by marriage, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.
en.R: You saw iron mixed with clay. This means that the people of this kingdom will try to unite through marriages between families, but they will not stay together, just as iron and clay do not mix.

fr.L: Et comme tu as vu le fer mêlé à l’argile de boue, ils se mêleront par la semence humaine, mais ils ne tiendront pas l’un à l’autre, de même que le fer ne se mêle pas à l’argile.
fr.B: Et comme tu as vu le fer mêlé à l’argile, ils se mêleront les uns aux autres par des mariages, mais ils ne tiendront pas ensemble, de même que le fer ne se mélange pas à l’argile.
fr.R: Tu as vu du fer mélangé à de l’argile. Cela veut dire que les gens de ce royaume essaieront de s’unir par des mariages entre familles, mais ils ne resteront pas unis, de même que le fer et l’argile ne se mélangent pas.

es.L: Y así como viste el hierro mezclado con el barro cenagoso, se mezclarán por medio de la simiente humana, pero no se unirán el uno con el otro, así como el hierro no se mezcla con el barro.
es.B: Y así como viste el hierro mezclado con el barro, así se mezclarán unos con otros por medio de matrimonios, pero no se mantendrán unidos, así como el hierro no se mezcla con el barro.
es.R: Viste hierro mezclado con barro. Eso significa que la gente de ese reino tratará de unirse por medio de matrimonios entre familias, pero no se mantendrá unida, así como el hierro y el barro no se mezclan.

decisions.choice: they will mix by the seed of men: they will try to unite by intermarriage
alternatives: a mixing of different peoples in the kingdom
decisions.reason: "Seed" means offspring, so the phrase most likely refers to marriages between ruling families, made to bind the parts of the kingdom together (compare the marriage alliances of 11:6, 17). They will fail. Some read it more widely, of a mixing of peoples within the kingdom.

decisions.choice: they will not cling to one another
decisions.reason: Like iron and clay, the parts of the kingdom will be joined but never truly united.

decisions.choice: by marriage (B); through marriages between families (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable state the most likely meaning of "the seed of men" (m1). Literal keeps the phrase.

source.text: וּֽבְיוֹמֵיה֞וֹן דִּ֧י מַלְכַיָּ֣א אִנּ֗וּן יְקִים֩ אֱלָ֨הּ שְׁמַיָּ֤א מַלְכוּ֙ דִּ֤י לְעָלְמִין֙ לָ֣א תִתְחַבַּ֔ל וּמַ֨לְכוּתָ֔ה לְעַ֥ם אָחֳרָ֖ן לָ֣א תִשְׁתְּבִ֑ק תַּדִּ֤ק וְתָסֵיף֙ כָּל־אִלֵּ֣ין מַלְכְוָתָ֔א וְהִ֖יא תְּק֥וּם לְעָלְמַיָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And in their days, of those kings, will set up the God of the heavens a kingdom which forever will not be destroyed, and the kingdom to a people another will not be left; it will shatter and bring to an end all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.

en.L: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will raise up a kingdom that forever will not be destroyed, and the kingdom will not be left to another people. It will shatter and bring to an end all these kingdoms, and it will stand forever.
en.B: In the time of those kings the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed. Its rule will never pass to another people. It will crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will itself endure forever.
en.R: While those kings are ruling, the God of heaven will start a kingdom that no one can ever destroy. No other people will ever take it over. It will crush all those other kingdoms and put an end to them. But it will last forever.

fr.L: Et aux jours de ces rois, le Dieu des cieux suscitera un royaume qui ne sera jamais détruit, et le royaume ne sera pas laissé à un autre peuple. Il brisera et anéantira tous ces royaumes, et lui-même subsistera à jamais.
fr.B: Au temps de ces rois, le Dieu des cieux établira un royaume qui ne sera jamais détruit. Sa royauté ne passera jamais à un autre peuple. Il écrasera tous ces royaumes et y mettra fin, mais lui-même durera à jamais.
fr.R: Pendant que ces rois régneront, le Dieu du ciel fera naître un royaume que personne ne pourra jamais détruire. Aucun autre peuple ne pourra jamais s’en emparer. Il écrasera tous ces autres royaumes et les fera disparaître. Mais lui, il durera pour toujours.

es.L: Y en los días de esos reyes, el Dios de los cielos levantará un reino que jamás será destruido, y el reino no será dejado a otro pueblo; desmenuzará y pondrá fin a todos estos reinos, y permanecerá para siempre.
es.B: En el tiempo de esos reyes, el Dios de los cielos establecerá un reino que nunca será destruido. Su dominio nunca pasará a otro pueblo. Aplastará a todos estos reinos y les pondrá fin, pero él mismo permanecerá para siempre.
es.R: Mientras esos reyes estén gobernando, el Dios de los cielos comenzará un reino que nadie podrá destruir jamás. Ningún otro pueblo se adueñará de él. Destrozará a todos esos otros reinos y acabará con ellos. Pero ese reino durará para siempre.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed
decisions.reason: This is the heart of the dream: after the human kingdoms, God will establish his own kingdom, which no one will take from his people and which will last forever. The same hope returns in 4:31; 6:27; 7:14, 18, 27. Jesus' preaching of "the kingdom of God" (Mark 1:15) takes up this hope.

decisions.choice: in the days of those kings: while the kingdoms of the dream still stand
alternatives: the rulers of the divided fourth kingdom only
decisions.reason: "Those kings" may be the kings of the fourth kingdom, or of all four kingdoms seen as one statue, struck down together (verse 35).

decisions.choice: the God of heaven at every level
decisions.reason: The title is kept at every level, as in verse 18.

source.text: כָּל־קֳבֵ֣ל דִּֽי־חֲזַ֡יְתָ דִּ֣י מִטּוּרָא֩ אִתְגְּזֶ֨רֶת אֶ֜בֶן דִּי־לָ֣א בִידַ֗יִן וְ֠הַדֶּקֶת פַּרְזְלָ֨א נְחָשָׁ֤א חַסְפָּא֙ כַּסְפָּ֣א וְדַהֲבָ֔א אֱלָ֥הּ רַב֙ הוֹדַ֣ע לְמַלְכָּ֔א מָ֛ה דִּ֥י לֶהֱוֵ֖א אַחֲרֵ֣י דְנָ֑ה וְיַצִּ֥יב חֶלְמָ֖א וּמְהֵימַ֥ן פִּשְׁרֵֽהּ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Because that you saw that from the mountain was cut out a stone which [was] not by hands, and it shattered the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold. A God great has made known to the king what will be after this; and certain [is] the dream, and trustworthy its interpretation.

en.L: Because you saw that from the mountain a stone was cut out, not by hands, and that it shattered the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold, a great God has made known to the king what will be after this. And the dream is certain, and its interpretation trustworthy."
en.B: This is the meaning of the stone you saw cut out of the mountain, not by human hands, which smashed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold. A great God has shown the king what is to come. The dream is certain, and its interpretation can be trusted."
en.R: You saw a rock cut out of a mountain, but no human hand cut it. The rock smashed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold. The great God has shown you, Your Majesty, what will happen in the future. The dream is true, and you can be sure of what it means."

fr.L: Puisque tu as vu que de la montagne s’est détachée une pierre, non par des mains, et qu’elle a brisé le fer, le bronze, l’argile, l’argent et l’or, un grand Dieu a fait connaître au roi ce qui arrivera après cela. Et le songe est certain, et son interprétation digne de foi. »
fr.B: C’est là le sens de la pierre que tu as vue se détacher de la montagne sans l’intervention d’aucune main humaine, et qui a broyé le fer, le bronze, l’argile, l’argent et l’or. Un grand Dieu a fait connaître au roi ce qui doit arriver. Le songe est certain, et son interprétation est sûre. »
fr.R: Tu as vu un rocher se détacher d’une montagne, mais aucune main humaine ne l’avait détaché. Le rocher a écrasé le fer, le bronze, l’argile, l’argent et l’or. Le grand Dieu t’a montré, ô roi, ce qui va arriver dans l’avenir. Le rêve est vrai, et tu peux être sûr de ce qu’il veut dire. »

es.L: Por cuanto viste que del monte fue cortada una piedra, no con manos, y que desmenuzó el hierro, el bronce, el barro, la plata y el oro, el gran Dios ha hecho saber al rey lo que ha de suceder después de esto. Y el sueño es verdadero, y fiel su interpretación».
es.B: Este es el significado de la piedra que viste desprenderse del monte sin intervención de mano humana, y que hizo pedazos el hierro, el bronce, el barro, la plata y el oro. El gran Dios le ha mostrado al rey lo que va a suceder. El sueño es verdadero, y su interpretación es digna de confianza».
es.R: Viste que una roca se desprendió de una montaña, pero ninguna mano humana la cortó. La roca destrozó el hierro, el bronce, el barro, la plata y el oro. El gran Dios te ha mostrado a ti, mi rey, lo que va a pasar en el futuro. El sueño es verdadero, y puedes estar seguro de lo que significa».

decisions.choice: because you saw: the stone's meaning sums up the interpretation
decisions.reason: The verse may finish the sentence of verse 44 ("it will stand forever, just as you saw the stone ...") or begin a new one. Either way it links the stone of the dream with God's kingdom.

decisions.choice: a great God: God who is great
decisions.reason: Without the article, the phrase can be "a great God" or "the great God". Daniel speaks to a pagan king, who may hear it as one god among others; for Daniel it is the God of heaven.

decisions.choice: certain ... trustworthy: the dream will surely come true
decisions.reason: The two words assure the king that the future shown in the dream is fixed and that the interpretation is reliable.

decisions.choice: This is the meaning of the stone (B); separate sentences (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence, which the Aramaic allows (m1).

source.text: בֵּ֠אדַיִן מַלְכָּ֤א נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּר֙ נְפַ֣ל עַל־אַנְפּ֔וֹהִי וּלְדָנִיֵּ֖אל סְגִ֑ד וּמִנְחָה֙ וְנִ֣יחֹחִ֔ין אֲמַ֖ר לְנַסָּ֥כָה לֵֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Then the king Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face, and to Daniel he paid homage, and an offering and soothing [incenses] he said to offer to him.

en.L: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and paid homage to Daniel, and he said to offer to him an offering and soothing [incenses].
en.B: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell face down and bowed before Daniel, and he ordered that an offering and incense be presented to him.
en.R: Then King Nebuchadnezzar bowed down to the ground in front of Daniel to honor him. He ordered his servants to give Daniel an offering and to burn incense for him.

fr.L: Alors le roi Nabuchodonosor tomba sur sa face et se prosterna devant Daniel, et il dit de lui offrir une offrande et des [parfums] apaisants.
fr.B: Alors le roi Nabuchodonosor tomba face contre terre et se prosterna devant Daniel, et il ordonna qu’on lui présente une offrande et de l’encens.
fr.R: Alors le roi Nabuchodonosor s’est incliné jusqu’à terre devant Daniel pour l’honorer. Il a ordonné à ses serviteurs de donner une offrande à Daniel et de brûler de l’encens pour lui.

es.L: Entonces el rey Nabucodonosor cayó sobre su rostro y se postró ante Daniel, y mandó que le ofrecieran ofrenda e incienso [de olor grato].
es.B: Entonces el rey Nabucodonosor cayó rostro en tierra y se inclinó ante Daniel, y ordenó que le presentaran una ofrenda e incienso.
es.R: Entonces el rey Nabucodonosor se inclinó hasta el suelo delante de Daniel para honrarlo. Ordenó a sus siervos que le dieran a Daniel una ofrenda y que quemaran incienso en su honor.

decisions.choice: paid homage: bowed in reverence
decisions.reason: The verb means to bow down, whether in worship of a god (3:5-7) or in honor of a person. The offerings suggest that the king treated Daniel as a god's representative, or even as divine. The text does not say whether Daniel accepted it; in verse 47 the king's praise is given to Daniel's God.

decisions.choice: an offering and soothing incenses
decisions.reason: The first word is a gift or grain offering; the second is the "soothing" or "pleasing aroma" of sacrifices and incense (Ezra 6:10; Leviticus 1:9).

decisions.choice: bowed before (B); bowed down ... to honor him (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the act without saying "worshiped", which would settle a question the text leaves open (m1).

source.text: עָנֵה֩ מַלְכָּ֨א לְדָנִיֵּ֜אל וְאָמַ֗ר מִן־קְשֹׁט֙ דִּ֣י אֱלָהֲכ֗וֹן ה֣וּא אֱלָ֧הּ אֱלָהִ֛ין וּמָרֵ֥א מַלְכִ֖ין וְגָלֵ֣ה רָזִ֑ין דִּ֣י יְכֵ֔לְתָּ לְמִגְלֵ֖א רָזָ֥ה דְנָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Answering the king to Daniel and saying: from truth that your God he [is] God of gods and Lord of kings and revealer of secrets, because you have been able to reveal this secret.

en.L: The king answered Daniel and said, "In truth, your God is God of gods and Lord of kings and a revealer of secrets, for you have been able to reveal this secret."
en.B: The king said to Daniel, "Your God is truly the God above all gods and the Lord over kings, and one who reveals mysteries, for you have been able to reveal this mystery."
en.R: The king said to Daniel, "Your God is surely the greatest God of all and the Lord over all kings. He shows people secrets, because you were able to tell me this secret."

fr.L: Le roi répondit à Daniel et dit : « En vérité, votre Dieu est le Dieu des dieux et le Seigneur des rois, et celui qui révèle les mystères, puisque tu as pu révéler ce mystère. »
fr.B: Le roi dit à Daniel : « Votre Dieu est vraiment le Dieu qui est au-dessus de tous les dieux et le Seigneur des rois, celui qui révèle les mystères, puisque tu as pu révéler ce mystère. »
fr.R: Le roi a dit à Daniel : « Votre Dieu est vraiment le plus grand de tous les dieux et le Seigneur de tous les rois. Il fait connaître les secrets aux gens, puisque tu as pu me dire ce secret. »

es.L: Respondió el rey a Daniel y dijo: «Ciertamente el Dios de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es Dios de dioses y Señor de reyes, y el que revela los misterios, pues pudiste revelar este misterio».
es.B: El rey le dijo a Daniel: «Verdaderamente el Dios de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es el Dios por encima de todos los dioses y el Señor de los reyes, y el que revela los misterios, porque tú pudiste revelar este misterio».
es.R: El rey le dijo a Daniel: «Sin duda el Dios de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es el Dios más grande de todos y el Señor de todos los reyes. Él da a conocer los secretos, pues tú pudiste decirme este secreto».

decisions.choice: God of gods and Lord of kings: the king confesses the greatness of Daniel's God
decisions.reason: "God of gods" means the greatest God (Deuteronomy 10:17; Psalm 136:2). The king's confession is real but limited: he still speaks as a polytheist, and in chapter 3 he sets up his own image. The title "revealer of secrets" takes up Daniel's words in verses 28-29.

decisions.choice: the greatest God of all (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the Aramaic way of saying "greatest" ("God of gods").

decisions.choice: "votre Dieu" (plural): the king speaks of the God of Daniel and his companions
decisions.reason: The Aramaic possessive is plural; French can show it, where the English "your" cannot.

source.text: אֱדַ֨יִן מַלְכָּ֜א לְדָנִיֵּ֣אל רַבִּ֗י וּמַתְּנָ֨ן רַבְרְבָ֤ן שַׂגִּיאָן֙ יְהַב־לֵ֔הּ וְהַ֨שְׁלְטֵ֔הּ עַ֖ל כָּל־מְדִינַ֣ת בָּבֶ֑ל וְרַב־סִגְנִ֔ין עַ֖ל כָּל־חַכִּימֵ֥י בָבֶֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Then the king Daniel made great, and gifts great [and] many he gave to him, and he made him ruler over all [the] province of Babylon and chief of [the] prefects over all [the] wise men of Babylon.

en.L: Then the king made Daniel great, and great gifts, many, he gave to him; and he made him ruler over all the province of Babylon, and chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.
en.B: Then the king promoted Daniel and gave him many great gifts. He made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief prefect in charge of all the wise men of Babylon.
en.R: Then the king gave Daniel a high position and many fine gifts. He made him ruler of the whole province of Babylon and put him in charge of all the wise men of Babylon.

fr.L: Alors le roi éleva Daniel, et il lui donna de grands présents, nombreux ; et il le fit dominer sur toute la province de Babylone, et [le fit] chef des préfets sur tous les sages de Babylone.
fr.B: Alors le roi éleva Daniel à un haut rang et lui fit de nombreux et riches présents. Il le fit gouverneur de toute la province de Babylone et chef des préfets, à la tête de tous les sages de Babylone.
fr.R: Alors le roi a donné à Daniel un poste très important et beaucoup de beaux cadeaux. Il l’a fait gouverneur de toute la province de Babylone et l’a mis à la tête de tous les sages de Babylone.

es.L: Entonces el rey engrandeció a Daniel, y le dio muchos y grandes regalos, y lo hizo gobernador de toda la provincia de Babilonia y jefe de los prefectos sobre todos los sabios de Babilonia.
es.B: Entonces el rey ascendió a Daniel y le dio muchos y grandes regalos. Lo puso como gobernador de toda la provincia de Babilonia y jefe principal de todos los sabios de Babilonia.
es.R: Entonces el rey le dio a Daniel un puesto muy alto y muchos regalos valiosos. Lo hizo gobernador de toda la provincia de Babilonia y lo puso a cargo de todos los sabios de Babilonia.

decisions.choice: the province of Babylon ... chief of the prefects
decisions.reason: The province of Babylon was the region around the capital. The word for "prefects" is a title for high officials (3:2-3; 6:8). Daniel is given authority both in government and over the class of wise men whose lives he had saved.

decisions.choice: made Daniel great: as Pharaoh raised Joseph
decisions.reason: Like Joseph, who interpreted Pharaoh's dreams and was set over Egypt (Genesis 41:39-43), Daniel the Judean exile is raised to high office.

decisions.choice: chief prefect in charge of (B); put him in charge (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says that the office gave Daniel charge of the wise men; Readable says only that, leaving out the title.

source.text: וְדָנִיֵּאל֙ בְּעָ֣א מִן־מַלְכָּ֔א וּמַנִּ֗י עַ֤ל עֲבִֽידְתָּא֙ דִּ֚י מְדִינַ֣ת בָּבֶ֔ל לְשַׁדְרַ֥ךְ מֵישַׁ֖ךְ וַעֲבֵ֣ד נְג֑וֹ וְדָנִיֵּ֖אל בִּתְרַ֥ע מַלְכָּֽא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And Daniel asked from the king, and he appointed over the administration of [the] province of Babylon Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego; and Daniel [was] in [the] gate of the king.

en.L: And Daniel asked the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego over the administration of the province of Babylon; and Daniel [was] at the gate of the king.
en.B: Daniel made a request of the king, and the king put Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in charge of the affairs of the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained at the royal court.
en.R: Daniel asked the king to give his three friends, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, important jobs too. So the king put them in charge of the affairs of the province of Babylon. But Daniel stayed at the king's palace.

fr.L: Et Daniel fit une demande au roi, et il établit Shadrak, Méshak et Abed-Nego sur l’administration de la province de Babylone ; et Daniel [était] à la porte du roi.
fr.B: À la demande de Daniel, le roi confia à Shadrak, Méshak et Abed-Nego l’administration de la province de Babylone, tandis que Daniel restait à la cour du roi.
fr.R: Daniel a demandé au roi de donner aussi des postes importants à ses trois amis, Shadrak, Méshak et Abed-Nego. Alors le roi les a chargés de diriger les affaires de la province de Babylone. Mais Daniel est resté au palais du roi.

es.L: Y Daniel pidió al rey, y él puso sobre la administración de la provincia de Babilonia a Sadrac, Mesac y Abed-nego; y Daniel [estaba] a la puerta del rey.
es.B: A petición de Daniel, el rey puso a Sadrac, Mesac y Abed-nego a cargo de los asuntos de la provincia de Babilonia, mientras que Daniel permaneció en la corte real.
es.R: Daniel le pidió al rey que también les diera puestos importantes a sus tres amigos, Sadrac, Mesac y Abed-nego. Así que el rey los puso a cargo de los asuntos de la provincia de Babilonia. Pero Daniel se quedó en el palacio del rey.

decisions.choice: in the king's gate: at the royal court
decisions.reason: The gate of a city or palace was where officials sat and business was done (Esther 2:19, 21). Daniel served at the center of power, while his friends governed the province. This prepares for chapter 3, where the three stand without Daniel.

decisions.choice: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego: the Babylonian names of 1:7
decisions.reason: In matters of the court the friends are named by their Babylonian names, as in chapter 3.

decisions.choice: his three friends ... important jobs too (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly who the three are and what Daniel asked for.
